docs.title: promptise.mcpcast.wizard.probe_local_apis(*, ports=PROBE_PORTS, paths=PROBE_PATHS, timeout=0.4, read_timeout=2.0, budget=DETECT_BUDGET, max_bytes=DETECT_MAX_BYTES, fetch=None, cancelled=None)
docs.text:
Look for OpenAPI documents served by APIs running on this machine.

Probes http://127.0.0.1:<port><path> for every port and path (first hit per port wins) and keeps the ones that parse as an OpenAPI document with at least one operation. Loopback only, GET only, redirects not followed, bodies parsed strictly (never fetched or read as a path), capped at max_bytes and held to the node budget and nesting depth :func:~promptise.mcpcast.parse.load_spec enforces, every string scrubbed of terminal control characters (see :func:_parse_document); whatever a probed service answers, a malformed or hostile body is skipped, never raised. Probing stops once budget seconds have passed — the ports not reached are reported, not silently dropped.

docs.title: Memory API Reference
docs.text: Agent memory integration layer with auto-injection. Provides a MemoryProvider protocol and adapters for external memory backends (Mem0, ChromaDB) plus a lightweight InMemoryProvider for testing. The key feature is auto-injection: MemoryAgent wraps any LangGraph agent and transparently prepends relevant memories to every invocation.

docs.title: promptise.memory.MemoryProvider
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Interface for memory backends.

All methods are async. Implementations must handle their own thread-safety and connection management. Callers should call :meth:close when the provider is no longer needed.

Multi-user isolation is controlled by the scope passed to the concrete provider (see :class:MemoryScope). When scope is PER_USER, every mutating / querying call must carry a user_id so the provider can partition entries. When scope is SHARED the user_id parameter is ignored.

docs.title: promptise.memory.InMemoryProvider
docs.text:
Keyword-search memory provider for testing.

Stores entries in a dictionary. Search ranks entries that contain the whole query first, then entries by the share of the query's words they contain (case-insensitive, common stop words ignored). Entries that share no word with the query are not returned. There are no embeddings, so synonyms do not match — not suitable for production.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_entries int

Maximum stored entries. When exceeded, oldest entries are evicted (FIFO).

10000 scope MemoryScope | None

Isolation mode. SHARED (default) lets every caller see every entry. PER_USER partitions entries by user_id — search / delete only operate on rows the caller owns.

None

docs.title: promptise.memory.ChromaProvider
docs.text:
Adapter for ChromaDB <https://www.trychroma.com/>_.

Requires pip install chromadb (or pip install "promptise[all]"). Provides local vector similarity search with automatic embedding generation. ChromaDB handles its own input validation internally.

Scores. New collections are created with cosine distance (metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}), and a result's :attr:MemoryResult.score is its cosine similarity (1 - distance, clamped to [0, 1]). A collection that already exists keeps the distance function it was created with — Chroma cannot change it — and the score is derived from that function: ip uses 1 - distance, and l2 (Chroma's default, used by collections created by Promptise 1.2.1 and earlier) uses 1 - distance / 2, which equals cosine similarity for unit-length embeddings such as Chroma's default model. A warning is logged for an l2 collection; re-create it to get cosine distances (see the memory guide).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default collection_name str

Name of the ChromaDB collection.

'agent_memory' persist_directory str | None

Path for persistent storage. When None, uses an ephemeral in-memory client.

None embedding_function Any

Custom ChromaDB embedding function. When None, uses ChromaDB's default (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via Sentence Transformers).

None scope MemoryScope | None

Isolation mode (see :class:MemoryScope).

None

Raises:

Type Description ImportError

If chromadb is not installed.

provider = ChromaProvider(
    collection_name="agent_memory",
    persist_directory=".promptise/chroma",
)
await provider.add("User prefers dark mode")
results = await provider.search("theme preferences")

docs.title: close() async
docs.text:
Release ChromaDB client resources.

After calling close(), any further operations will raise RuntimeError. ChromaDB's PersistentClient does not expose an explicit close method, so we null references to allow garbage collection.

docs.text:
List entries whose metadata matches metadata exactly.

Runs a ChromaDB get(where=...); see :meth:InMemoryProvider.list_entries. Order is ChromaDB's.

docs.text:
Delete every Chroma entry owned by user_id (of tenant_id).

Uses ChromaDB's delete(where=...) filter to drop all rows in a single round-trip. Returns 0 for SHARED-scope providers.

docs.title: promptise.memory.Mem0Provider
docs.text:
Adapter for mem0 <https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0>_.

Requires pip install mem0ai (or pip install "promptise[all]"). Supported releases: mem0ai>=0.1.118,<3 (the 0.1, 1.x and 2.x lines). Wraps Mem0's hybrid retrieval (vector + optional graph search) behind the :class:MemoryProvider protocol.

Mem0 changed its Python API between major versions: from 2.0, Memory.search() and Memory.get_all() take the entity ids in a filters dict and the result count as top_k (and reject user_id= / limit=), while 0.1 and 1.x take user_id= / agent_id= / limit=. The adapter reads the installed client's search() signature once and calls whichever form it accepts. Memory.add() takes the text as messages in every supported release.

Mem0 can run fully local (with Ollama) or via their cloud platform. Pass a config dict to from_config() for self-hosted setups.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default user_id str

Scopes memories to a user (required by Mem0).

'default' agent_id str | None

Optional agent identifier for multi-agent scoping.

None config dict[str, Any] | None

Optional Mem0 configuration dict. Passed directly to mem0.Memory.from_config(). If None, uses Mem0 defaults.

None scope MemoryScope | None

Isolation mode (see :class:MemoryScope).

None

Raises:

Type Description ImportError

If mem0ai is not installed.

provider = Mem0Provider(user_id="user-42")
await provider.add("User prefers dark mode")
results = await provider.search("theme preferences")

docs.title: close() async
docs.text:
Release Mem0 client resources. Stored memories are kept.

Calls the client's close() when it has one, then drops the reference. After calling close(), any further operations will raise RuntimeError.

In 1.4.3 and earlier this called Mem0's Memory.reset(), which deletes every stored memory (the vector store collection and the history database), so closing a provider (AgentProcess.close(), async with, removing a runtime process) wiped the memories it was meant to keep. To delete memories on purpose, use :meth:delete / :meth:purge_user, or Mem0's own API.

docs.title: list_entries(*, user_id=None, metadata=None, limit=1000) async
docs.text:
List the user's entries whose metadata matches metadata exactly.

Uses Mem0's get_all (up to limit entries, in the API form the installed release accepts -- see :meth:search) and filters client-side. See :meth:InMemoryProvider.list_entries.

docs.title: purge_user(user_id, *, tenant_id=None) async
docs.text:
Delete every Mem0 entry owned by user_id (of tenant_id).

Counts the user's entries with get_all and removes them with Mem0's delete_all(user_id=...); when delete_all is missing or fails, deletes the listed entries one by one. Returns 0 for SHARED-scope providers and when no entries existed.

scope=PER_USER and no user_id.

Whatever the Mem0 client raises. Errors are not turned into an empty result, so an incompatible Mem0 release or an unreachable vector store is visible.

docs.title: promptise.memory.MemoryAgent
docs.text:
Wraps an agent with automatic memory context injection.

Before every :meth:ainvoke, searches the memory provider for content relevant to the user's query and injects matching results as a SystemMessage. The agent sees relevant context without needing explicit memory tools.

If the memory provider fails (timeout, connection error), the agent continues normally without memory context — memory never blocks execution.

Composable with :class:PromptiseAgent::

MemoryAgent(PromptiseAgent(graph), provider)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default inner Any

The wrapped LangGraph agent (Runnable).

required provider MemoryProvider

A :class:MemoryProvider implementation.

required max_memories int

Maximum results to inject per invocation.

5 min_score float

Minimum relevance score threshold (0.0--1.0).

0.0 timeout float

Maximum seconds to wait for memory search.

5.0 auto_store bool

If True, automatically store each exchange (user input + agent output) after invocation completes.

False

docs.text:
Sanitize memory content before injection into agent messages.

Strips known prompt-injection patterns and fence markers so that recalled memory cannot hijack the agent's instruction context. Content is also truncated to a safe injection length.

Uses case-insensitive regex matching with whitespace tolerance to catch pattern variations like "SyStEm :" or "SYSTEM:".

Note

docs.title: Models API Reference
docs.text:
Bring your own model: promptise.models is the one place that turns a model description into a LangChain chat model. Every entry point that accepts a model -- build_agent(model=...), .superagent and .agent files, promptise mcpcast --model, the CLI's --model-id -- goes through resolve_model(), so the friendly provider names (azure, foundry, gemini, vertex, bedrock, mistral, grok, hf, ...) and the same actionable errors apply everywhere. The promptise models CLI and the provider table in the docs are generated from the same registry, so the code, the CLI and the pages cannot disagree.

Nothing to install per provider. OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Anthropic use their native integrations, which are part of the core install; every other provider is reached through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint with langchain-openai, also core. Model(..., native=True) opts into a provider's own LangChain package when you have installed it yourself.

There are three ways to say which model and how to reach it, and they share one vocabulary:

  1. A string -- "provider:model"; credentials come from the environment or a .env file: build_agent(model="azure:chat-prod").
  2. A Model -- provider, model and credentials in code, in the shape of LangChain's init_chat_model: Model("gpt-4o", provider="azure", deployment="chat-prod", endpoint=..., api_key=..., api_version=...). The words are the same for every provider.
  3. A config file -- the same fields under model: in a .superagent file.

Any LangChain BaseChatModel instance is accepted too, for full control.

import asyncio
from promptise import Model, build_agent, check_model, resolve_model, ModelSetupError

# Diagnose without calling anything
result = check_model("azure:chat-prod")
if not result.ok:
    print("\n".join(result.problems))   # each problem names its fix

# Or let resolution raise a ModelSetupError with the same text
try:
    llm = resolve_model("groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile")
except ModelSetupError as exc:
    print(exc)   # GROQ_API_KEY is not set: console.groq.com → API Keys ... put it in .env, export it, or pass api_key=

async def main():
    # A string: build_agent() calls resolve_model() for you; .env or env vars supply the credentials
    agent = await build_agent(model="azure:chat-prod", instructions="Be concise.")
    await agent.shutdown()

    # A Model: provider, model and credentials in code
    agent = await build_agent(
        model=Model(
            "gpt-4o",
            provider="azure",
            deployment="chat-prod",
            endpoint="https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/",
            api_key="...",
            api_version="2024-10-21",
            temperature=0,
        ),
        instructions="Be concise.",
    )
    await agent.shutdown()

asyncio.run(main())

For the walkthrough -- Azure AI Foundry in depth, every provider, custom and self-hosted endpoints -- see Model Setup; for where keys live, Configuration & Secrets.

docs.title: promptise.models.resolve_model(spec, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Turn a "provider:model" string (plus optional words) into a chat model.

Keyword arguments are the :class:Model words (api_key, endpoint, deployment, api_version, region, project), the settings (temperature, max_tokens, timeout), native=True, and any provider-specific extras, which are passed through. A word that is None or a blank string counts as not given, so the environment (or .env) supplies it — api_key="" never shadows the credential check.

Raises:

Type Description ModelSetupError

Naming each missing variable and where to find it, the word that does not apply to the provider, or a .env file that cannot be read.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
How the words reach a provider: for the three native integrations they map to that class's own arguments (endpoint → azure_endpoint= on Azure OpenAI, base_url= on OpenAI and Anthropic; deployment → azure_deployment=). For every other provider the words build the OpenAI-compatible request: endpoint overrides the provider's default URL (or is the URL for Azure AI Foundry and Ollama), region and project fill the URL template for Bedrock and Vertex AI, api_version sets Azure AI Foundry's api-version query parameter, and api_key becomes the bearer token (Bedrock: a Bedrock API key; Vertex AI: an OAuth access token — minted for you when google-auth and Application Default Credentials are available, as a token provider the client calls before every request, so the ~1 h token is refreshed before it expires; a token given by hand is used as given and expires). A word a provider has no setting for raises ModelSetupError with what to use instead; a word that is None or a blank string counts as not given (an empty api_key="" never shadows the environment check). extra is merged in last, verbatim -- a keyless Azure OpenAI setup is Model("gpt-4o", provider="azure", deployment=..., endpoint=..., api_version=..., extra={"azure_ad_token_provider": provider}).

>>> Model("m", provider="groq", deployment="d").resolve()
ModelSetupError: Groq has no 'deployment' setting: only Azure OpenAI addresses models by deployment name — put the name in model=.

docs.title: promptise.models.Model dataclass
docs.text:
Provider, model and credentials in code — the LangChain shape.

Positional model is what the model is ("gpt-4o"); provider is where it runs ("azure", "openai", "foundry", "bedrock"… — any prefix or alias from :data:PROVIDERS, inferred from the model name like LangChain does when omitted); deployment is what you named it there (Azure OpenAI). The remaining words are the same for every provider. Anything else goes in extra verbatim. A value given here counts as provided, so the matching environment variable is not required; None or a blank string (api_key="" — what ${OPENAI_API_KEY} yields for a variable exported but empty) counts as not given, and the environment or .env supplies it.

Model("azure:chat-prod") — the string form inside Model — means Model("chat-prod", provider="azure").

repr() and str() never include api_key or extra, so a Model is safe to log and to name in error messages.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model str

The model name (Azure OpenAI: the underlying model, e.g. "gpt-4o"; the request goes to deployment).

required provider str | None

Provider prefix or alias. Omit it to let LangChain infer the provider from the model name (gpt-… → OpenAI).

None deployment str | None

Azure OpenAI deployment name — what you called the model when you deployed it in Azure AI Foundry. Defaults to model.

None api_key str | None

The provider's key (Bedrock: a Bedrock API key; Vertex AI: an OAuth access token; not applicable to a local Ollama).

None endpoint str | None

Where to send requests — an Azure OpenAI resource endpoint, an Azure AI Foundry inference endpoint, or the /v1 URL of any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, a proxy, a NIM…). For providers with a public API this overrides the default URL.

None api_version str | None

Azure OpenAI REST API version ("2024-10-21"), or the Azure AI Foundry inference api-version.

None region str | None

Bedrock region or Vertex AI location.

None project str | None

Google Cloud project id (Vertex AI).

None temperature float | None

Sampling temperature.

None max_tokens int | None

Completion token limit.

None timeout float | None

Request timeout in seconds.

None native bool

Use the provider's native LangChain integration instead of its OpenAI-compatible endpoint (langchain-aws for IAM auth on Bedrock, langchain-google-genai for Gemini-only features…). The package must be installed; nothing is installed for you.

False extra dict[str, Any]

Provider-specific keyword arguments passed through untouched ({"azure_ad_token_provider": ...}, {"default_headers": {...}}).

dict() 
Model("gpt-5-mini", provider="openai", api_key="sk-...")
Model("gpt-4o", provider="azure", deployment="chat-prod",
      endpoint="https://r.openai.azure.com/", api_key="...", api_version="2024-10-21")
Model("Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct", provider="foundry",
      endpoint="https://r.services.ai.azure.com/models", api_key="...")
Model("anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0", provider="bedrock",
      region="us-east-1", api_key="ABSK...")
Model("qwen2.5", provider="openai", endpoint="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="none")

docs.title: ModelSetupError
docs.text:
The message always says what to do. Missing credentials, nothing set:

Cannot use model azure:'chat-prod' (Azure OpenAI (OpenAI models deployed in Azure AI Foundry)) yet:
  - AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT is not set: Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Overview → Endpoint (https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/, no path) (e.g. https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/)
  - AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY is not set: Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Keys and Endpoint → KEY 1 (or Entra ID: pass extra={'azure_ad_token_provider': ...})
  - OPENAI_API_VERSION is not set: the REST API version your deployment supports, e.g. 2024-10-21 (Azure docs → 'API version lifecycle') (e.g. 2024-10-21)
  - put AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_VERSION in a .env file next to your script (loaded automatically, never overrides a set variable), export it, or pass it in code: Model(..., endpoint=, api_key=, api_version=). See promptise models env azure
  Model part means: in the string form, your DEPLOYMENT name (Foundry → Deployments → Name); with Model(...), the model name (gpt-4o); the deployment goes in deployment=.
  Example: azure:chat-prod
  Diagnose any model string with: promptise models check azure:chat-prod

Bases: RuntimeError

A model cannot be used yet — the message says exactly what to do.

docs.title: load_dotenv_if_present
docs.text: The search is bounded and the file is checked before it is read: the walk from the working directory stops after the project root (the first ancestor holding pyproject.toml or .git), and a candidate that is not a regular file or -- on POSIX -- is owned by another user or world-writable is skipped with a UserWarning that names it. A file that cannot be read or is not UTF-8 raises ModelSetupError naming the path (cannot read /path/.env: ... — fix its permissions/encoding, move it, or set PROMPTISE_NO_DOTENV=1) — the same error resolve_model(), build_agent() and the CLI surface, never a raw PermissionError. The promptise CLI loads the file once, in its global callback, and prints .env loaded from <path> on stderr.

docs.title: promptise.models.load_dotenv_if_present(*, cwd=None)
docs.text:
Load the nearest safe .env file from cwd (default: the working directory) upward.

The search walks from cwd through its parents and stops after the project root — the first directory holding pyproject.toml or .git — so a file above the project (/tmp/.env on a shared host, another user's home) is never consulted. A candidate is loaded only when it is a regular file and, on POSIX, owned by you and not world-writable; anything else is skipped with a :class:UserWarning naming the file (once per process) and the search continues upward.

A variable that is already set to a non-empty value is never overwritten. A variable exported as an empty string (export OPENAI_API_KEY= left in a shell profile) counts as unset everywhere in this module, so the file's non-empty value fills it — python-dotenv alone would skip it and the key would look "not set" although it is in the file. Empty values in the file set nothing. :func:dotenv_origin reports which file filled a variable.

Returns the path that was loaded, or None. Set PROMPTISE_NO_DOTENV=1 to disable (tests and hermetic deployments). Loading happens once per process per file; call again after os.chdir to pick up another one.

Raises:

Type Description ModelSetupError

When the file that would be loaded cannot be read or is not UTF-8 — the message names it and says what to do.

docs.title: dotenv_origin

from promptise.models import dotenv_origin, load_dotenv_if_present

load_dotenv_if_present()
dotenv_origin("OPENAI_API_KEY")   # '/home/me/project/.env' — or None when the shell set it

promptise models check uses it to print set (from /home/me/project/.env) next to every variable the file filled.

docs.title: promptise.observability.ObservabilityCollector
docs.text:
Thread-safe collector for structured timeline events.

Records events from agents, tools, prompts, and the runtime. Events are dispatched to registered :class:BaseTransporter instances in real time. Supports ring-buffer eviction via max_entries.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default session_name str

Human-readable label for this session.

'promptise' max_entries int

Maximum number of entries to retain. Oldest entries are evicted when the buffer is full. Defaults to 100,000.

100000 sanitizer Callable[[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any]] | None

Optional callable applied to every event before it is stored or sent to a transporter: it gets the event's metadata, and {"details": <text>} for its details, and returns the cleaned dict. :func:redact_sensitive is the one :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent uses. None (default) records events unchanged.

None 
collector = ObservabilityCollector("my-agent-session")
collector.add_transporter(ConsoleTransporter())

entry = collector.record(
    TimelineEventType.TOOL_CALL,
    agent_id="my-agent",
    details="Calling search_files",
    metadata={"tool_name": "search_files"},
)

docs.text:
One observed agent invocation, from agent.input to agent.output.

:class:~promptise.agent.PromptiseAgent opens a run for every invocation it observes and makes it current for the duration of the call. While a run is current, :meth:ObservabilityCollector.record sets each event's parent_id to :attr:entry_id (unless one is passed explicitly), which is what links LLM turns, tool calls and cache events to the invocation that caused them — the OpenTelemetry transporter builds its span tree from it. The callback handler also adds the run's token usage and call counts here, so agent.output can report per-invocation totals.

docs.title: promptise.observability.redact_sensitive(metadata)
docs.text:
Replace credentials and common PII in event metadata with placeholders.

The sanitizer :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent installs on the collector it creates (ObservabilityConfig.redact_sensitive, on by default), so tool arguments, tool results, error messages and recorded prompt text cannot carry secrets into reports, log files or exported traces. It uses the same patterns as the event notifier: API keys (OpenAI/Anthropic sk-…, Stripe, Google), AWS access key IDs and secret access keys, GitHub tokens (ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_, github_pat_), GitLab and Slack tokens, JWTs, PEM private keys, Bearer tokens and every Authorization value (any scheme), credentials in URLs (://user:password@), card numbers, US social security numbers and email addresses. The value of a credential key (Authorization, password, api_key, access_token...) is replaced whatever it looks like.

String values are scrubbed at any depth; other values (numbers, flags) are kept as they are. Pattern matching cannot recognise every kind of personal data (names, addresses), so set record_tool_io=False and leave record_prompts off when traces leave your trust boundary.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default metadata dict[str, Any]

Event metadata (or any JSON-like dict).

required

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, Any]

A new dict with sensitive substrings replaced.

docs.text:
Configuration for the observability system.

Pass as observe=config to :func:build_agent or use the shorthand observe=True for sensible defaults.

Examples::

# Defaults: STANDARD level, HTML transporter
ObservabilityConfig()

# Enterprise: full detail, multiple transporters
ObservabilityConfig(
    level=ObserveLevel.FULL,
    record_prompts=True,
    transporters=[
        TransporterType.HTML,
        TransporterType.STRUCTURED_LOG,
        TransporterType.CONSOLE,
        TransporterType.PROMETHEUS,
    ],
    output_dir="./observability",
    log_file="./logs/events.jsonl",
    console_live=True,
    correlation_id="req-abc-123",
)

Whether to store prompt, response, agent input and output text (truncated to 2,000 characters) in event metadata.

None (default) follows :attr:level: on at FULL, off below it. True records text at any level; False never records it, even at FULL.

docs.title: record_tool_io = True class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
Whether to store tool arguments (tool.call) and result previews (tool.result) in event metadata, truncated to 2,000 characters.

On by default — arguments and results are what make a trace debuggable. Tool arguments often carry user data (names, emails, account numbers), so set False when traces leave your trust boundary: events then keep the tool name, latency and error status, plus arguments_length and result_length. Independent of :attr:record_prompts.

Applies to the collector :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent creates; a collector passed as observer= keeps its own sanitizer. On by default; set False only when traces stay inside your trust boundary.

docs.title: promptise.observability_config.ObserveLevel
docs.text:
Bases: str, Enum

Controls how much detail the observability system captures.

  • OFF: nothing. The agent still has a (permanently empty) collector, so agent.get_stats() and timeline queries keep working, but no events are recorded and no transporters are created.
  • BASIC: agent.input / agent.output / agent.error per invocation (agent.output carries the run's token totals), tool calls and results, LLM and tool errors, cache events.
  • STANDARD: BASIC plus llm.start / llm.end for every LLM turn, with token usage, latency and the tools the model asked for.
  • FULL: STANDARD plus prompt, response, agent input and output text (unless record_prompts=False) and streamed-token counts.

Tool arguments and results are controlled separately by :attr:ObservabilityConfig.record_tool_io.

docs.title: BASIC = 'basic' class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Agent input/output, tool calls, errors and cache events; no per-LLM-turn events.

docs.title: FULL = 'full' class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Everything in STANDARD plus prompt/response content and streaming tokens.

docs.title: OFF = 'off' class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Observability disabled: nothing is recorded.

docs.title: STANDARD = 'standard' class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Everything in BASIC plus every LLM turn with token usage and latency.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseTransporter

Bridges timeline events to Prometheus metrics.

Auto-creates and increments counters and histograms:

  • promptise_llm_calls_total (counter: agent_id, model)
  • promptise_llm_tokens_total (counter: agent_id, token_type)
  • promptise_llm_duration_seconds (histogram: agent_id, model)
  • promptise_tool_calls_total (counter: agent_id, tool_name)
  • promptise_tool_duration_seconds (histogram: agent_id, tool_name)
  • promptise_tool_errors_total (counter: agent_id, tool_name)
  • promptise_events_total (counter: event_type, category)

If the prometheus_client package is not installed, metrics are tracked internally as plain Python dicts (accessible via :attr:metrics).

Port for the Prometheus /metrics HTTP endpoint. If set to 0, no HTTP server is started. Default: 0 (no server).

docs.title: promptise.observability_transporters.OTLPTransporter
docs.text:
Bases: BaseTransporter

Exports agent runs to OpenTelemetry as traces, via OTLP gRPC.

Each agent invocation becomes one trace: an invoke_agent span from agent.input to agent.output (or agent.error), with a chat <model> child span per LLM call (llm.start → llm.end) and an execute_tool <name> child span per tool call (tool.call → tool.result / tool.error). Spans carry the real start and end times of the work, so their duration is the latency. Other events recorded during the run (cache hits, retries, approvals …) become span events on the run span; events outside a run become standalone spans.

If an OpenTelemetry span is active when the agent is invoked (for example the server span of an instrumented web framework), the run span becomes its child, so the agent run joins the request's trace.

Attributes follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions where one exists (gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens, gen_ai.tool.name) plus enduser.id and session.id from the :class:~promptise.agent.CallerContext, promptise.correlation_id, and each event's scalar metadata as promptise.<key>. Failed LLM calls, tool calls and runs get an ERROR status.

Requires the [all] extra::

pip install "promptise[all]"

Compatible with Jaeger, Datadog, Honeycomb, Grafana Tempo, and any OTLP-compatible backend.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default endpoint str

OTLP gRPC endpoint. Default: "http://localhost:4317".

'http://localhost:4317' service_name str

OpenTelemetry service name. Default: "promptise".

'promptise' correlation_id str | None

Optional ID added to every span as promptise.correlation_id.

None tracer_provider Any | None

An existing TracerProvider to emit spans through (for example your application's). When given, endpoint and service_name are not used and the provider is flushed but not shut down by :meth:close. When omitted, a private provider with an OTLP exporter is created; the global tracer provider is never replaced.

None

docs.title: promptise.callback_handler.PromptiseCallbackHandler
docs.text:
Bases: BaseCallbackHandler

LangChain callback handler → ObservabilityCollector bridge.

Captures every LLM turn, tool call, token count, latency, retry, and error. Designed to be the only integration point needed between LangChain's event system and Promptise's observability.

What is recorded depends on level (see :class:~promptise.observability_config.ObserveLevel): OFF records nothing, BASIC skips the per-turn llm.start / llm.end events (token usage is still added to the current agent run), STANDARD records every turn, and FULL also records prompt and response text unless record_prompts=False.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default collector Any

The :class:~promptise.observability.ObservabilityCollector.

required agent_id str | None

Agent identifier stamped on every event.

None record_prompts bool | None

Record prompt and response text. None follows level (on at FULL only); True / False force it.

None level ObserveLevel

Detail level.

STANDARD record_tool_io bool

Record tool arguments and result previews. When False, only their lengths are recorded.

True

docs.title: promptise.prompts.core.Prompt
docs.text:
Dual-mode prompt: standalone LLM caller + agent instruction source.

Wraps a function whose docstring is the prompt template. Decorated with @prompt(model=...) to create a Prompt instance.

Standalone mode — await prompt("text")::

result = await analyze("quarterly report")

Agent-integrated mode — render without LLM call::

text = await prompt.render_async(ctx)  # full prompt text
messages = await prompt.to_messages(ctx)  # LangChain messages

All with_*() methods return copies (immutable composition).

docs.title: promptise.prompts.blocks.Block
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

A composable unit of prompt content.

Implement this protocol to create custom block types. The priority determines survival when token budgets are tight (10 = always included, 1 = nice-to-have).

Three ways to create custom blocks:

  1. Class: Implement the Block protocol::

    class MyBlock: name = "my_block" priority = 5 def render(self, ctx=None) -> str: return "Custom content"

  2. @block decorator: Turn a function into a block::

    @block("my_block", priority=5) def my_block(ctx=None) -> str: return "Custom content"

  3. SimpleBlock: Inline with just a string::

    my_block = SimpleBlock("my_block", "Custom content", priority=5)

docs.title: promptise.prompts.context.BaseContext
docs.text:
Extensible context container.

Accepts arbitrary keyword arguments. Predefined subclasses add typed convenience fields but NEVER restrict what developers can store.

Example::

# Predefined fields
user = UserContext(user_id="123", name="Alice")

# Custom fields — no subclassing needed
user = UserContext(user_id="123", department="eng", clearance="high")

# Entirely custom context
project = BaseContext(sprint="2026-Q1", budget=50000)

# Access
project.sprint            # "2026-Q1"
project["budget"]         # 50000
project.get("missing")    # None

# Extend after creation
project.deadline = "March 2026"

# Merge
combined = project.merge(BaseContext(team_size=5))

docs.title: render(template, variables)
docs.text:
Render template with variables.

Processing order:

  1. {% include "name" %} — resolved from includes registry
  2. !`shell command``` — replaced with stdout (only if ashell_executorwas provided to the engine; otherwise the syntax is left as-is). The output is literal text: braces in it are kept as they are, never read asor`` syntax.
  3. {% if condition %}...{% else %}...{% endif %} — truthiness
  4. {% for item in items %}...{% endfor %} — iteration
  5. {{ / }} — literal brace escapes
  6. {variable} — interpolation via :meth:str.format_map

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

A referenced variable is missing from variables.

ValueError

An {% include %} references an unknown name.

ShellExecutionError

A `cmd block fails (only when a shell executor is configured).

docs.title: promptise.prompts.template.ShellExecutor
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Protocol for objects that can run a templated shell command.

Implementations must be callable with a single string (the command) and return its stdout as a string. They are responsible for enforcing any sandboxing, timeouts, or allowlists.

docs.title: promptise.prompts.template.SubprocessShellExecutor
docs.text:
Default shell executor backed by :func:subprocess.run.

Runs the command via the system shell with a timeout. Captures stdout and returns it stripped. Stderr and a non-zero exit code raise :class:ShellExecutionError.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float

Max seconds the command may run before being killed. Default 5.0.

5.0 shell bool

Whether to invoke through /bin/sh -c. Default True (matches the `cmd ergonomic). Ignored when an allowlist is set: allowlisted commands never run through a shell.

True cwd str | None

Working directory for the subprocess. Default None (inherits caller's cwd).

None env dict[str, str] | None

Optional environment variables to merge in.

None allowlist set[str] | None

Optional set of executable names that are allowed to run. When set, the command is split into words like a shell would (:func:shlex.split), its first word must be one of these names exactly ("git" does not allow /usr/bin/git), and it is run directly, without a shell. Shell syntax is refused rather than passed on: a command with an unquoted operator (;, |, &, <, >, (, )) raises :class:ShellExecutionError, so echo hi; rm -rf ~ cannot run a second command. The arguments of an allowlisted command are not checked: allow only commands that cannot do harm whatever arguments they get (git with -c, find with -exec can run other programs).

None

Raised when a templated shell command fails or times out.

docs.title: RAG API Reference
docs.text:
The promptise.rag module provides a pluggable foundation for retrieval-augmented generation: base classes you subclass for your loader, chunker, embedder, and vector store, plus a pipeline orchestrator and LangChain tool adapter.

See the RAG guide for architecture overview and usage patterns.

docs.title: promptise.rag.Document dataclass
docs.text:
A raw document loaded from a data source.

A Document is the input to the RAG pipeline. It holds the full text and metadata but has not been chunked or embedded yet.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

Stable identifier for the document. Used for updates and deletes. If your source doesn't have one, hash the URL or file path.

text str

The full text content of the document.

metadata dict[str, Any]

Arbitrary structured metadata. Typical fields include source, url, title, author, created_at. Metadata is copied to every chunk derived from the document so retrieval results include provenance.

Attributes:

Unique chunk identifier. Typically derived from the document id and chunk index (e.g. doc-1:chunk-0).

The parent document's identifier.

The chunk text content.

Vector representation. None until an embedder populates it. VectorStore implementations can assume this is set when :meth:VectorStore.add is called.

metadata dict[str, Any]

Copied from the parent document, plus any chunk-level fields the chunker adds (e.g. chunk_index, page).

docs.title: promptise.rag.DocumentLoader
docs.text:
Fetches raw documents from a data source.

Subclass this for each source you need to index: filesystem, S3, Confluence, Notion, Postgres, a REST API, etc. Implementations should return a list (or async iterator) of :class:Document instances with stable id fields so re-indexing is idempotent.

Example::

class MarkdownFolderLoader(DocumentLoader):
    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.path = path

    async def load(self) -> list[Document]:
        from pathlib import Path
        docs = []
        for p in Path(self.path).rglob("*.md"):
            docs.append(Document(
                id=str(p.relative_to(self.path)),
                text=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                metadata={"source": str(p), "filename": p.name},
            ))
        return docs

Subclass this if you need special chunking logic (preserve code blocks, respect markdown headers, split by semantic boundaries, etc). For most use cases, :class:RecursiveTextChunker is sufficient.

Implementations must preserve the parent document's metadata on every chunk and can add chunk-level metadata (e.g. chunk_index, char_start, char_end, page).

docs.title: promptise.rag.Embedder
docs.text:
Converts text into vector embeddings.

Subclass this to wrap any embedding provider (OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage, sentence-transformers, a local model, etc).

Implementations should:

  • Support batching via :meth:embed for efficiency.
  • Return vectors of consistent dimensionality (check with :attr:dimension).
  • Handle retries and rate limiting internally.

Example::

class SentenceTransformersEmbedder(Embedder):
    def __init__(self, model_name: str = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"):
        from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
        self._model = SentenceTransformer(model_name)

    async def embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        return await loop.run_in_executor(
            None, lambda: self._model.encode(texts).tolist()
        )

    @property
    def dimension(self) -> int:
        return self._model.get_sentence_embedding_dimension()

docs.title: promptise.rag.VectorStore
docs.text:
Persists embedded chunks and performs similarity search.

Subclass this for your vector database: Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, PGVector, Redis, Elasticsearch, or a custom backend.

All methods are async. Implementations are responsible for:

  • Serializing chunk metadata to whatever format the backend needs (all vector DBs have slightly different metadata constraints).
  • Converting native similarity scores into the [0.0, 1.0] range expected by :class:RetrievalResult.
  • Handling connection lifecycle (pooling, reconnection, shutdown).

Example::

class QdrantStore(VectorStore):
    def __init__(self, url: str, collection: str):
        from qdrant_client import AsyncQdrantClient
        self._client = AsyncQdrantClient(url=url)
        self._collection = collection

    async def add(self, chunks: list[Chunk]) -> None:
        points = [
            {
                "id": c.id,
                "vector": c.embedding,
                "payload": {"text": c.text, **c.metadata},
            }
            for c in chunks
        ]
        await self._client.upsert(self._collection, points=points)

    async def search(self, vector, *, limit=5, filter=None):
        res = await self._client.search(
            self._collection, query_vector=vector, limit=limit,
            query_filter=filter,
        )
        return [
            RetrievalResult(
                chunk=Chunk(
                    id=hit.id,
                    document_id=hit.payload.get("document_id", ""),
                    text=hit.payload.get("text", ""),
                    metadata={k: v for k, v in hit.payload.items() if k != "text"},
                ),
                score=hit.score,
            )
            for hit in res
        ]

    async def delete(self, chunk_ids: list[str]) -> None:
        await self._client.delete(self._collection, points_selector=chunk_ids)

docs.title: promptise.rag.RecursiveTextChunker
docs.text:
Bases: Chunker

Split text into fixed-size chunks with overlap.

Uses a hierarchy of separators — double newlines (paragraph breaks), then single newlines, then sentence boundaries, then word boundaries — to keep chunks readable. Adds chunk-level metadata (chunk_index, char_start, char_end) and preserves the parent document's metadata.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default chunk_size int

Target characters per chunk.

500 overlap int

Number of characters shared between consecutive chunks to preserve context across boundaries. Set to ~10-20% of chunk_size for most use cases.

50 separators list[str] | None

Ordered list of separator patterns to try. Defaults to [" ", " ", ". ", " "]. When none of them splits a piece small enough, the piece is cut into chunk_size-character windows that share overlap characters. An empty string "" in the list means that character-level cut.

None

docs.title: promptise.rag.InMemoryVectorStore
docs.text:
Bases: VectorStore

Reference vector store that keeps everything in memory.

Uses brute-force cosine similarity against a list of stored chunks. Suitable for testing, small demo corpora, and as a reference implementation to copy when building your own :class:VectorStore.

Scores are cosine similarity mapped from [-1, 1] onto [0, 1] as (cosine + 1) / 2, so an unrelated (orthogonal) chunk scores 0.5. Metadata filters match exactly: every key must be present on the chunk with an equal value. Chunks are copied on the way in and out, so changing a returned result never changes the stored chunk.

For production, adapt the methods to Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, etc. The interface is the same — only the backend changes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dimension int | None

Expected embedding dimension. When set, :meth:add raises if a chunk's embedding has the wrong length, and :meth:search raises if the query vector has the wrong length.

None

docs.title: promptise.rag.RAGPipeline
docs.text:
Orchestrates the full RAG flow: load → chunk → embed → store → retrieve.

A pipeline wires together four components (loader, chunker, embedder, store) into a single object that agents can treat as a black box. The same pipeline interface works whether you're using an in-memory store for tests or a managed Pinecone cluster in production.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default loader DocumentLoader | None

:class:DocumentLoader that fetches source documents.

None chunker Chunker | None

:class:Chunker that splits documents into chunks. Defaults to :class:RecursiveTextChunker with 500-char chunks.

None embedder Embedder

:class:Embedder that converts text to vectors. Required.

required store VectorStore

:class:VectorStore that persists and searches vectors. Required.

required batch_size int

Number of chunks to embed in a single call to :meth:Embedder.embed. Tune based on your embedding provider's rate limits.

64 
pipeline = RAGPipeline(
    loader=MarkdownFolderLoader("./docs"),
    embedder=OpenAIEmbedder(),
    store=PineconeStore("my-index"),
)
report = await pipeline.index()
print(f"Indexed {report.chunks_stored} chunks in {report.duration_seconds:.1f}s")

hits = await pipeline.retrieve("password reset")
for hit in hits:
    print(f"[{hit.score:.2f}] {hit.text[:80]}")

docs.title: promptise.rag.rag_to_tool(pipeline, *, name='search_knowledge_base', description='Search the knowledge base for information relevant to a query.', limit=5, format='markdown')
docs.text:
Wrap a :class:RAGPipeline as a LangChain tool the agent can call.

The returned tool has a query argument and an optional limit. When the LLM invokes it, the pipeline embeds the query, retrieves the top limit chunks, and formats them for display.

Retrieved text is untrusted: anyone who can put text in an indexed document can write instructions aimed at the model. The tool output therefore says that the results are data, not instructions. In the "markdown" and "text" formats the results sit inside a block delimited by a random tag generated for each call, so a document can't close the block early; the "json" format returns {"notice": ..., "results": [...]}.

Every caller of the agent searches the same pipeline: the tool does not scope results to the caller. Index only documents that every caller may read, or see the RAG guide for scoping retrieval per caller.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default pipeline RAGPipeline

The RAG pipeline to wrap.

required name str

Tool name the LLM sees. Make it specific — e.g. "search_product_docs" or "search_support_tickets".

'search_knowledge_base' description str

Tool description the LLM uses to decide when to call it. Be clear about what's in the knowledge base.

'Search the knowledge base for information relevant to a query.' limit int

Default number of results per query (at least 1). The tool exposes this as a parameter so the LLM can override it for broad vs. narrow searches.

5 format str

How to format results: "markdown" (default, human and LLM friendly), "json" (structured), or "text" (plain).

'markdown'

Returns:

Type Description Any

A LangChain StructuredTool ready to pass to build_agent

Any

via the extra_tools parameter.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If format is not one of the three formats or limit is less than 1.

from promptise import build_agent
from promptise.rag import rag_to_tool

docs_tool = rag_to_tool(
    pipeline,
    name="search_internal_docs",
    description="Search Acme Corp's internal engineering wiki.",
)

agent = await build_agent(
    model="openai:gpt-5-mini",
    servers={},
    extra_tools=[docs_tool],
)

docs.title: Runtime API Reference
docs.text: Agent process lifecycle, triggers, governance (budget, health, mission, secrets), journals, distributed coordination, and the orchestration API.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.process.AgentProcess
docs.text:
Lifecycle container for a long-running agent process.

Lifecycle (see :mod:promptise.runtime.lifecycle): :meth:start, :meth:stop, :meth:suspend / :meth:resume, automatic restarts (restart_policy) and :meth:close. Every lifecycle change emits an event when an event_notifier is set: process.started, process.stopped, process.failed (with the error), process.restarted, process.restart_exhausted, process.suspended and process.resumed (both with a reason: "manual", "idle", "budget", "health", "rewind" or, for an automatic resume, "trigger").

Trigger events are processed in arrival order. While the process is suspended they wait in the queue; at :meth:stop the events still queued (or held by a worker, or running) are moved to :attr:dead_letters with reason "process stopped", from where :meth:redeliver_dead_letters can queue them again after a restart.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str

Unique process name.

required config ProcessConfig

Process configuration.

required process_id str | None

Unique ID (auto-generated if not provided).

None event_bus Any | None

Optional shared EventBus for inter-process events.

None broker Any | None

Optional shared MessageBroker for message triggers.

None runtime Any | None

Optional parent :class:AgentRuntime reference (enables the spawn_process meta-tool in open mode).

None event_notifier Any | None

Optional :class:~promptise.events.EventNotifier for the process's events (and its agent's).

None hooks HookManager | None

Optional shared :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookManager (e.g. one :class:AgentRuntime passes to all its processes), dispatched after the process's own :attr:hooks (which holds config.hooks); ctx.process_id names the process.

None deploy_policy DeployPolicy | None

Where the config came from (:class:~promptise.runtime._deploy_policy.DeployPolicy). The default is an operator config without limits; the control API passes source="api", which limits ${VAR} references in secrets to the variables the operator allowed and makes an empty open_mode.allowed_mcp_urls mean no MCP server. Processes this one spawns get the same policy.

None extra_tools Sequence[Any] | None

Local tools for the agent, added after config.extra_tools (same kinds as :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent's extra_tools: :func:promptise.tool functions, plain functions and LangChain tools). They go through the same budget, approval, health and journal checks as MCP tools and are kept on every rebuild of the agent. Anything that is not a tool raises TypeError here.

None model Any | None

The agent's model, used instead of config.model: a model id, or a model object as :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent takes it (a LangChain chat model such as promptise.testing.ScriptedModel, a :class:promptise.Model, a :class:~promptise.FallbackChain). Every agent the process builds uses it, and so does the mission evaluator. Anything else raises ValueError here.

None

Lifecycle hooks: the process dispatches every :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookEvent to :attr:hooks (see the event's docstring for when, with which data, and what blocking it does). Hook data has secret values redacted.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

An entry of config.servers is not a server spec (see :func:_resolve_server_specs), or model is not a model.

TypeError

An entry of extra_tools is not a tool or function.

docs.text: The unified agent context.

docs.title: dead_letters property
docs.text:
Trigger events that could not be processed, oldest first.

Each entry has event (the :class:TriggerEvent), reason ("retries exhausted", "process failed", "process stopped", "process restarting", "trigger removed", "queue full", "flagged by payload scan", "blocked by guardrails" or "blocked by hook"), error, attempts and dead_lettered_at. A stop dead-letters every event not run yet: queued, held by a worker or a trigger listener, or still inside a trigger (a file watch's backlog, a webhook's accepted requests). The list keeps the most recent trigger_delivery.dead_letter_size entries.

docs.title: hooks property
docs.text:
This process's :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookManager.

Holds the hooks of config.hooks; register more in code::

@process.hooks.on(HookEvent.USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT)
async def audit(ctx):
    ...

Its default hook timeout is 30 seconds. A hook must not await a lifecycle method of this process (stop(), start(), rewind()); schedule it with asyncio.create_task.

docs.text:

The new process is registered in the parent :class:AgentRuntime and started; it inherits this process's guardrails (see :meth:_child_config), its hooks (the parent's :attr:hooks, and what the parent itself inherited, are dispatched for the child after its own, so permission_request and user_prompt_submit hooks govern the child too) and its deploy policy (a child of an API-deployed process is limited like its parent). docs.title: stop(*, drain_timeout=0.0) async
docs.text:
Transitions: RUNNING / SUSPENDED / STARTING / FAILED → STOPPING → STOPPED (emits process.stopped), or CREATED → STOPPED for a process that never started (no event). Stopping a stopped process does nothing.

Trigger events still queued, held by a suspended worker or running are moved to :attr:dead_letters (reason "process stopped"). A run in flight is cancelled at once by default. With drain_timeout the stop is graceful: no new event starts (the triggers' events and :meth:inject go to the dead letters, a webhook answers 503), the runs in flight get up to that many seconds to finish, and only the ones still running then are cancelled.

A cancelled run's event (error "run cancelled") may have had tool calls with effects already. It is journaled as a run_interrupted entry and kept in the journal checkpoint, so the next process object with the same name and journal lists it in :attr:dead_letters again after :meth:start.

Secrets are revoked unless secrets.revoke_on_stop is False. Long-term memory, the context state and the conversation history are kept (unless context.conversation_clear_on_stop), so a later :meth:start continues where this one stopped; :meth:close releases them.

An explicit stop also cancels any pending automatic restart.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default drain_timeout float | None

Seconds to let runs in flight finish before cancelling them. 0 (default) cancels them at once; None uses config.drain_timeout (what :meth:AgentRuntime.run_forever does on SIGTERM).

0.0

Manages a dictionary of :class:AgentProcess instances with shared resources and coordinated lifecycle.

The processes declared in config.processes are registered at construction (not started): AgentRuntime(config) and :meth:from_config are equivalent.

docs.text:
Start all processes and run until shutdown is requested.

Returns after :meth:request_shutdown, SIGTERM or SIGINT (with install_signal_handlers), or when the task running it is cancelled; every process is then stopped and closed (:meth:shutdown), so docker stop or Ctrl+C never cuts a process off without process.stopped, a final checkpoint and its dead letters.

The stop is graceful: no new trigger event starts, and runs in flight get up to drain_timeout seconds to finish before they are cancelled (a cancelled run is journaled, see :meth:AgentProcess.stop). A second signal during that wait cancels them at once.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default install_signal_handlers bool

Install SIGTERM / SIGINT handlers on the running loop for the duration of the call (removed afterwards: SIGTERM goes back to the default, SIGINT to KeyboardInterrupt). Skipped where the loop doesn't support them (Windows, or a thread other than the main one).

True drain_timeout float | None

Seconds runs in flight may take to finish at shutdown. None (default) uses each process's config.drain_timeout (5 seconds unless set); 0 cancels them at once. request_shutdown(drain_timeout=...) replaces it for that shutdown.

None

Trigger configurations.

AgentContext configuration.

Max concurrent trigger invocations.

Heartbeat period in seconds.

Seconds of inactivity before suspending (0 = never).

Max process lifetime in seconds (0 = unlimited).

Consecutive failures before FAILED state.

When to restart the process automatically. on_failure restarts it after it enters FAILED (e.g. max_consecutive_failures reached); always also restarts it when it stops itself at max_lifetime. An explicit :meth:~AgentProcess.stop never triggers a restart.

Seconds a graceful stop lets runs in flight finish before cancelling them (default 5). :meth:AgentRuntime.run_forever (SIGTERM, SIGINT) and stop(drain_timeout=None) use it; a plain :meth:~AgentProcess.stop cancels at once. Keep it below the platform's kill deadline (docker stop sends SIGKILL after 10 seconds by default).

max_restarts int

Max consecutive restart attempts after failures. The count resets after a successful invocation.

restart_backoff float

Delay in seconds before the first restart attempt; doubles on each consecutive attempt (capped at 60s).

Retries, dead-letter list and payload scanning for trigger events.

guardrails Any | None

Passed through to :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent when the agent is built, as are observe, cache, optimize_tools, adaptive and max_invocation_time.

Runtime lifecycle hooks (:class:HookConfig), registered on the process's :attr:~AgentProcess.hooks manager when the process is created.

Local tools the agent can call next to the MCP servers' tools, as in :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent: functions made tools with :func:promptise.tool, plain functions (made tools as if decorated with @tool) and LangChain BaseTool instances. Budget, approval, health and journal apply to them as to MCP tools, and every rebuild of the agent (restart, hot reload, new instructions) keeps them. Code only, like :attr:HookConfig.callback: not serialised (to_dict() and model_dump() leave them out), and a manifest or YAML config can't set them. Anything that is not a tool raises TypeError when the config is created.

Unknown keys are rejected, so a misspelt option fails loudly instead of being ignored.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.config.DistributedConfig
docs.text:
Bases: _WarnOnUnknownKeys

Distributed runtime coordination (RuntimeConfig.distributed).

With enabled=True, :meth:AgentRuntime.start_all (and :meth:~AgentRuntime.run_forever) start this node's management transport (:class:~promptise.runtime.distributed.RuntimeTransport) on transport_host:transport_port; :meth:AgentRuntime.shutdown stops it. Then, depending on the role:

  • coordinator=True: this runtime hosts the cluster coordinator (:class:~promptise.runtime.distributed.RuntimeCoordinator), which monitors the nodes' health. With discovery_method="registry" nodes register themselves at POST /cluster/nodes of its transport (and are dropped when they stop re-registering for node_timeout seconds); with "static" the nodes are listed in static_nodes. The coordinator also lists itself.
  • coordinator_url set: this node registers with the coordinator at that URL when it starts, re-registers every heartbeat_interval seconds (so a restarted coordinator finds it again) and unregisters at shutdown.
  • Neither: a stand-alone node, managed through its transport (a static coordinator elsewhere can list it).

Security: one cluster token (auth_token) authenticates everything: requests to this node's transport (every route but GET /health), this node's registration with the coordinator, and the coordinator's requests to the nodes. A non-loopback transport_host or a coordinator on another host needs it, unless allow_unauthenticated=True says a proxy or a private network authenticates callers.

Attributes:

Name Type Description enabled bool

Start the transport (and coordination) with the runtime.

coordinator bool

This runtime hosts the coordinator.

coordinator_url str | None

Base URL of the coordinator's transport, for discovery_method="registry" nodes.

node_id str | None

This node's ID (default: <hostname>-<port>).

transport_host str

Interface the transport binds (default loopback).

transport_port int

Port of the transport (0: a free port).

advertise_url str | None

URL other nodes reach this one at (default http://<transport_host>:<port>; required when binding a wildcard address and registering with a coordinator).

auth_token SecretStr | None

The cluster bearer token, or an ${ENV_VAR} reference resolved when the transport starts.

allow_unauthenticated bool

Allow a non-loopback transport or coordinator without auth_token.

discovery_method Literal['registry', 'static', 'multicast']

"registry" (nodes register with the coordinator) or "static" (static_nodes). "multicast" is not implemented and is rejected.

static_nodes dict[str, str]

node_id -> URL of the nodes, for a static coordinator.

allowed_node_hosts list[str]

For a registry coordinator: the host names or IP addresses a registering node's URL may name (*. + a domain matches its subdomains). Empty: any host. The coordinator sends the cluster token to every registered URL (health checks, management calls), so a token holder could point it anywhere; list your nodes' hosts to stop that.

heartbeat_interval float

Seconds between the coordinator's health checks and between a node's re-registrations.

node_timeout float | None

Seconds without a successful health check (or a re-registration) before a node counts as unhealthy (or is dropped from the registry). Default 3 * heartbeat_interval.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

An inconsistent combination (each message says what to change). In 1.4.3 and earlier these fields were read by nothing.

Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.config.OpenModeConfig
docs.text:
Bases: _WarnOnUnknownKeys

Guardrails for open execution mode.

Controls what the agent is allowed to self-modify and how far. Only takes effect when ProcessConfig.execution_mode is :attr:ExecutionMode.OPEN.

Security: open mode gives the model control over its own setup, so treat every allow_* capability as something the model (and whoever can put text in front of it: trigger payloads, inbox messages, tool results) can use. allow_tool_creation runs model-written Python inside the runtime's process; the restricted builtins are not a sandbox and can be escaped, so it amounts to running arbitrary code as the runtime's user. The control API refuses such deploys unless allow_command_deploys is on.

Attributes:

Name Type Description allow_identity_change bool

Agent can modify its own instructions.

allow_tool_creation bool

Agent can define new Python tools, executed in the runtime's process (not isolated; see above).

allow_mcp_connect bool

Agent can connect to new MCP servers.

allow_trigger_management bool

Agent can add/remove triggers.

allow_memory_management bool

Agent can explicitly store/search/forget.

max_custom_tools int

Max number of agent-created tools.

max_dynamic_triggers int

Max number of dynamically added triggers.

max_instruction_length int

Max character length for modified instructions.

max_rebuilds int | None

Max agent rebuilds (hot reloads) per lifetime of the process object; restarts do not reset it. A change the limit refuses is not applied, now or after a restart. rollback() is not refused. None = unlimited.

allowed_mcp_urls list[str]

The MCP server URLs the agent may connect to. Empty means any public URL for an operator-configured process (loopback, private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused; a warning is logged at start) and none for a process deployed through the control API. Listed URLs are trusted as written, private addresses included.

identity_mcp_urls list[str]

Agent-connected MCP servers that may receive the process identity's credential (identity) and a caller's token. Empty (the default): none do, so the agent can't send its credential to a server it picked.

sandbox_custom_tools bool

Run agent-written tools with restricted builtins and no imports (False: a fixed allowlist of standard-library imports). Either way the code runs in the runtime's process; this is not a security boundary.

allow_process_spawn bool

Agent can spawn new processes within the runtime. Defaults to False.

max_spawned_processes int

Max number of processes this agent can spawn.

allow_public_webhooks bool

Webhook triggers the agent adds, or gives a process it spawns, may bind a non-loopback webhook_host (they must then set hmac_secret). False (default): such triggers are refused.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.config.TriggerConfig
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Configuration for a single trigger.

Each trigger type requires a different subset of fields. The :meth:_validate_trigger_fields model validator enforces this for built-in types, and rejects bad cron expressions, time zones, filter expressions and source ranges when the config is created rather than when the process first runs. Custom trigger types use the custom_config dict. Unknown keys are rejected, so a misspelt option fails loudly instead of being ignored.

Attributes:

Name Type Description type str

Trigger type (built-in or custom-registered via :func:~promptise.runtime.triggers.register_trigger_type).

cron_expression str | None

Cron expression (cron type only). Five fields, or six with a trailing seconds field ("* * * * * */10" fires every 10 seconds).

cron_timezone str | None

IANA time zone the cron expression is read in (cron only). None means UTC.

webhook_path str

URL path for the webhook endpoint (webhook only).

webhook_port int

Listening port (webhook only).

webhook_host str

Interface to bind (webhook only). Defaults to 127.0.0.1 (loopback); use 0.0.0.0 to accept requests from other machines.

hmac_secret SecretStr | None

Shared secret for request signatures (webhook only). When set, unsigned or wrongly signed requests get 401. With signature_scheme="telegram" it is the secret_token given to Telegram's setWebhook (1-256 characters: letters, digits, _ and -).

signature_scheme Literal['generic', 'github', 'stripe', 'telegram']

How the signature is computed and sent: generic (X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>), github (X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>), stripe (Stripe-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=<hex> over "<ts>.<body>") or telegram (X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token: <secret>, the secret itself, compared in constant time).

signature_header str | None

Header carrying the signature. Defaults to the scheme's standard header.

signature_tolerance int

Max age in seconds of a timestamped (stripe) signature, to stop replays.

allowed_sources list[str]

Client IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to call the webhook (empty = any). Others get 403.

webhook_max_body_bytes int

Largest request body the webhook accepts, in bytes (webhook only, default 1 MiB). Larger bodies get 413.

watch_path str | None

Directory to watch (file_watch only).

watch_patterns list[str]

Glob patterns (file_watch only), matched against the file name.

watch_events list[str]

Filesystem events to react to (file_watch only): any of created, modified, deleted, moved.

watch_debounce_seconds float

Window in which events for the same file are merged into one (file_watch only).

watch_recursive bool

Also watch subdirectories (file_watch only, default True).

watch_backend Literal['auto', 'watchdog', 'polling']

How changes are detected (file_watch only): "auto" (native OS notifications through watchdog when it is installed, otherwise polling), "watchdog" (fail if it isn't installed) or "polling" (scan the directory every watch_poll_interval seconds; use it for network shares and bind mounts, where OS notifications are unreliable).

watch_poll_interval float

Seconds between scans with the polling backend (file_watch only).

watch_max_pending_events int

How many changed files the trigger holds while the process is busy (file_watch only). Events wait for the process instead of being dropped; changes to a file that is already waiting are merged into its event. Only when this many different files are waiting is a new one dropped, with an error log and a count in FileWatchTrigger.dropped_events.

event_type str | None

EventBus event type string (event only).

event_source str | None

Optional source filter (event only).

topic str | None

MessageBroker topic (message only).

custom_config dict[str, Any]

Additional key-value configuration for custom trigger types.

filter_expression str | Callable[..., Any] | None

Cheap pre-filter evaluated before the agent runs (all types, optional). Either a safe expression string such as "payload['action'] == 'opened'" (see :mod:promptise.runtime.triggers.filters) or a callable that takes the :class:~promptise.runtime.triggers.base.TriggerEvent and returns a bool. Events that don't match are skipped.

trusted bool

Deliver this trigger's payloads to the agent as the user's request instead of as untrusted data (all types, default False). By default a payload is wrapped in a block the agent is told not to take instructions from; with trusted=True it is not, so whoever can send this trigger an event directs the agent as its user does. Use it only for a trigger whose sender is authenticated, such as a chat webhook with hmac_secret: a webhook trigger without hmac_secret can't be trusted (ValueError), and the process logs a warning for a trusted file_watch, event, message or custom trigger, whose senders it can't verify. The payload scan (scan_payloads) and guardrails still apply.

Setting an option that belongs to another built-in trigger type (for example watch_path on a cron trigger) is an error, since the trigger would ignore it.

Triggers produce :class:TriggerEvent objects that cause the agent process to invoke the agent. They run as background tasks and must be safely cancellable.

A trigger that buffers events may also implement drain_pending() -> list[TriggerEvent]: after :meth:stop, the process takes those events and dead-letters them (on a restart: queues them for the restarted process) instead of losing them.

HTTP webhook trigger.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

URL path to listen on (e.g. "/webhook").

'/webhook' port int

TCP port to bind to.

9090 host str

Host/IP to bind to. Defaults to "127.0.0.1" (loopback only). Set to "0.0.0.0" when external services or other nodes need to reach this webhook.

'127.0.0.1' hmac_secret str | None

Optional HMAC secret for signature verification. When set, requests without a valid signature get 401. Verification uses timing-safe comparison. Strongly recommended when host is not loopback. 300 allowed_sources list[str] | None

Optional predicate; events it rejects are answered with 200 {"status": "ignored"} and not queued.

Largest request body accepted, in bytes (default 1 MiB). Larger requests get 413 and are not queued.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.triggers.event.InProcessEventBus
docs.text:
An event bus that delivers to subscribers in the same Python process.

Implements what the runtime uses a bus for: subscribe / unsubscribe (event triggers) and emit (escalations with an event_type, :class:~promptise.events.EventBusSink). Nothing leaves the process: to reach other hosts, pass your own bus to :class:~promptise.runtime.AgentRuntime.

runtime = AgentRuntime(event_bus=bus)
await bus.emit("pipeline.error", {"job": "nightly"}, source="etl")

Attributes:

Name Type Description enabled bool

stuck_threshold int

Same tool+args N times in a row = stuck.

loop_window int

Tool calls to examine for loop detection.

loop_min_repeats int

empty_threshold int

N consecutive trivial final replies = anomaly.

empty_max_chars int

A final reply of at most this many characters (after stripping whitespace) is trivial. With the default 10, a 10-character reply counts as empty and an 11-character one doesn't; 0 counts only blank replies.

error_window int

Number of recent invocations the error rate is computed over. The rate is checked once the window is full.

error_rate_threshold float

An error rate at or above this (0–1) in a full window is an anomaly.

on_anomaly Literal['log', 'pause', 'escalate', 'stop']

What the process does when a run produced an anomaly (a health.anomaly event is emitted in every case): "log" logs it; "pause" suspends the process; "escalate" sends the escalation notification to escalation (when set) and suspends the process; "stop" stops the process.

cooldown float

Seconds before the same anomaly (same kind and same evidence: the same stuck call or loop) is reported again. Set 0 to report every repeat, e.g. for an in-run guard. :meth:HealthMonitor.clear_anomalies resets it.

escalation EscalationTarget | None

Escalation target for anomalies.

Window sizes can be changed on a running monitor (for example with PATCH /api/v1/processes/{name}/health); the monitor resizes its windows and keeps the recorded data. Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.health.HealthMonitor
docs.text:
Lightweight behavioral health analysis.

All detection methods are pure logic — no I/O, no LLM calls. The same anomaly is reported at most once per cooldown seconds, to avoid spam. "The same" means the same kind and the same evidence: the same repeated call (stuck), the same repeating sequence (loop), or the same signal (empty responses, error rate). A different stuck call or loop is a new anomaly and is reported at once.

To use the monitor as an in-run guard that acts on every repeat (a pre_tool hook that blocks the call while the agent is stuck), set cooldown=0: :meth:record_tool_call then returns the anomaly on each call that continues it.

Window sizes follow the config: when error_window, loop_window, stuck_threshold or empty_threshold change on the config object the monitor reads (as PATCH /health does), the windows are resized on the next recorded call, keeping the most recent data. Call :meth:apply_config to switch to a different :class:HealthConfig object.

The anomaly history keeps the latest :attr:MAX_ANOMALIES anomalies; the per-type counts in :meth:health_status count all of them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default config HealthConfig

Health monitoring configuration.

required process_id str

Owning process ID.

required

docs.title: apply_config(config)
docs.text:
Switch to config, resizing the windows and keeping the data.

The most recent tool calls, reply lengths and error flags are kept (as many as fit the new windows), as are the anomaly history and the cooldowns. The new thresholds apply from the next recorded call.

docs.title: begin_invocation()
docs.text:
Start a new invocation: forget the previous run's tool calls.

Stuck and loop detection look for repetition within a run. A scheduled agent that calls the same tool once per run (e.g. a queue check every minute) is behaving normally, so tool history does not carry over between invocations. Response lengths and the error window do carry over: "three empty replies in a row" and "half the recent runs failed" are cross-run signals.

docs.title: clear_anomalies()
docs.text:
Forget detected anomalies and reset their cooldowns.

After a clear, the next occurrence of any anomaly is reported at once (not only after cooldown), counts start from zero and the monitor reports healthy. The tool-call, reply-length and error windows are kept: they are evidence, not reports.

Returns:

Type Description int

The number of anomalies that were in the history.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.mission.MissionTracker
docs.text:
Tracks mission progress across invocations.

Handles evaluation scheduling, LLM-as-judge calls, programmatic checks, timeout/limit checking, and context prompt generation.

completed and failed are final: a judge verdict that arrives after the mission was failed (for example by POST /mission/fail while an evaluation was running) doesn't change it. Only an active mission can be paused; only a paused one resumed.

The tracker keeps the latest :attr:MAX_EVALUATIONS evaluations. Its state round-trips through :meth:to_dict and :meth:restore (or :meth:from_dict), so a process can carry the mission across a restart: invocation count, elapsed time, state, failure reason and evaluation history.

Parameters:

Mission configuration.

required process_id str

Owning process ID.

required journal JournalProvider | None

Optional journal provider for logging evaluations.

None success_check Callable[[MissionEvidence], bool | None] | None

Optional callable (MissionEvidence) -> bool | None. Return True for achieved, False for not achieved, None for inconclusive (fall through to LLM evaluator).

None

Remove all secrets from the in-memory store.

docs.title: promptise.runtime.inbox.MessageInbox
docs.text:
Async-safe inbox for human-to-agent messages.

Provides a bounded, priority-sorted queue with TTL-based expiry, per-sender rate limiting, and question/response tracking.

When the inbox holds max_messages messages, adding one removes an answered question if there is one, otherwise evicts the oldest message of the lowest priority present. Critical messages are never evicted, and a message is never added in place of one with a higher priority: if every message in the inbox is critical, or the new message has a lower priority than every evictable one, the new message is refused with :class:InboxFullError. The inbox never holds more than max_messages messages.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_messages int

Maximum messages in the inbox.

50 max_message_length int

Maximum characters per message; longer content is truncated.

2000 default_ttl float

Default time-to-live in seconds (0 = no expiry).

3600 max_ttl float

Maximum allowed TTL in seconds (0 = no cap).

86400 rate_limit_per_sender int

Maximum messages per sender per hour (messages without sender_id are not limited).

20 scanner Any | None

Optional guardrail scanner (an object with scan_text(text, direction=...) such as :class:~promptise.guardrails.PromptiseSecurityScanner, or with check_input(text)). When set, :meth:add refuses content it flags with :class:InboxMessageRejected.

None
