docs.title: Agent Observability
docs.text:
Track token usage and export execution traces across your agent systems.

from promptise import build_agent
from promptise.config import HTTPServerSpec

# Simple: turn on observability with defaults
agent = await build_agent(
    servers={"tools": HTTPServerSpec(url="http://localhost:8000/mcp")},
    model="openai:gpt-5-mini",
    observe=True,
)

result = await agent.ainvoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]})

print(agent.get_stats()["total_tokens"])
agent.generate_report("report.html")  # interactive HTML report, written to exactly this path
await agent.shutdown()                 # also writes ./reports/promptise-report-<timestamp>.html

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Promptise observability is plug-and-play. Set observe=True and every agent invocation, LLM turn, tool call, token count, latency, retry, cache hit, and error is captured automatically: the agent records each invocation itself, and a LangChain callback handler records what happens inside it. Events are routed to one or more transporters -- HTML reports, structured logs, console output, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, or custom webhooks.

docs.title: What gets recorded
docs.text:
Every invocation (ainvoke, chat, astream, astream_with_tools) is an agent run:

Event When Metadata agent.input The invocation starts input_length, model (+ input_preview when text is recorded) llm.start / llm.end Each LLM turn (STANDARD and FULL) model, latency_ms, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, tool_calls (+ prompt_preview / response_preview) tool.call A tool is called tool_name, arguments tool.result The tool returned tool_name, latency_ms, result_preview tool.error The tool failed — it raised, or an MCP server answered isError: true (e.g. a ToolError) tool_name, latency_ms, error_type, error llm.error, llm.retry An LLM call failed or was retried error_type, error, attempt cache.miss / cache.store / cache.hit Semantic cache activity scope, ttl agent.output The invocation finished duration_ms, the run's prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / total_tokens, llm_call_count, tool_call_count, error_count, cache_hit, output_length (+ output_preview) agent.error The invocation raised error_type, error, and the same run totals

Every event recorded during a run has parent_id set to the run's agent.input entry, so you can pull one request out of a busy timeline (collector.query(...) then filter on parent_id), and the OpenTelemetry transporter turns each run into one trace. Events also carry the caller's user_id and session_id (see Multi-User Attribution).

docs.title: ObservabilityConfig
docs.text:
For full control, pass an ObservabilityConfig instead of True:

from promptise import build_agent
from promptise.observability_config import ObservabilityConfig, ObserveLevel, TransporterType

config = ObservabilityConfig(
    level=ObserveLevel.FULL,
    session_name="production-audit",
    record_prompts=True,
    transporters=[
        TransporterType.HTML,
        TransporterType.STRUCTURED_LOG,
        TransporterType.CONSOLE,
    ],
    output_dir="./reports",
    log_file="./logs/agent.jsonl",
    console_live=True,
)

agent = await build_agent(
    servers={"tools": HTTPServerSpec(url="http://localhost:8000/mcp")},
    model="openai:gpt-5-mini",
    observe=config,
)

docs.title: ObserveLevel
docs.text:
Controls the detail level of captured events:

Level Captures ObserveLevel.OFF Nothing. The agent keeps an empty collector (so get_stats() still works) and creates no transporters. ObserveLevel.BASIC agent.input / agent.output / agent.error, tool calls and results, LLM and tool errors, cache events. No per-turn LLM events; agent.output carries the run's token totals, and get_stats() counts them. ObserveLevel.STANDARD Everything in BASIC + llm.start / llm.end for every LLM turn, with token usage, latency, and the tools the model asked for. Default. ObserveLevel.FULL Everything in STANDARD + prompt, response, agent input and output text (truncated to 2,000 characters), and streamed-token counts.

docs.title: What text is recorded
docs.text:
Two switches decide whether user and model text lands in your traces:

Setting Default Records record_prompts None — follow the level: on at FULL, off below prompt_preview / response_preview on LLM events, input_preview / output_preview on agent events. True records them at any level; False never does, even at FULL. record_tool_io True arguments on tool.call, result_preview on tool.result, error and traceback on tool.error. With False the events keep the tool name, latency and error type, plus arguments_length / result_length.

Tool arguments are on by default because they are what makes a trace debuggable — but they often carry user data (names, emails, account numbers). Set record_tool_io=False when traces leave your trust boundary (a hosted APM, a shared log pipeline). Cache events never copy the user's query into their text.

Whatever is recorded is scrubbed first: with redact_sensitive=True (the default) every event's metadata and details pass through promptise.observability.redact_sensitive before they are stored or reach a transporter, so the HTML report, the NDJSON stream, log files, webhooks and OpenTelemetry spans all get the redacted text:

Found in the text Becomes OpenAI and Anthropic keys (sk-…), Stripe keys (sk_live_…, rk_test_…), Google API keys (AIza…) [API_KEY] AWS access key IDs (AKIA…, temporary ASIA…) [AWS_KEY] An AWS secret access key after aws_secret_access_key= (or :) aws_secret_access_key=[AWS_SECRET] GitHub tokens: ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_ (including the longer ghs_<app id>_<JWT> installation tokens), ghr_, github_pat_ [GITHUB_TOKEN] GitLab tokens (glpat-, gldt-, glptt-, glrt-) and Slack tokens (xoxb-, xoxp-...) [GITLAB_TOKEN], [SLACK_TOKEN] JSON Web Tokens and PEM private keys [JWT], [PRIVATE_KEY] An Authorization value with any scheme, or none (Authorization: Basic …, authorization=…) Authorization: Basic [REDACTED] A bearer token wherever it appears (Bearer …, bearer …) Bearer [REDACTED] The value of a credential key (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, X-API-Key, api_key, access_token, refresh_token, id_token, client_secret, password, passwd), as a dict key or in JSON text [REDACTED] Passwords in URLs (postgres://user:pw@host), card numbers, US social security numbers, email addresses ://[REDACTED]@, [CARD], [SSN], [EMAIL]

Pattern matching cannot recognise names, addresses or credentials without a known format or label, so it complements record_tool_io=False rather than replacing it. When an agent run fails on a guardrail, agent.error records the direction, the number of blocked findings and their categories, never the matched text.

The redaction applies to the collector build_agent() creates. A collector you pass as observer= keeps its own sanitizer — pass ObservabilityCollector(sanitizer=redact_sensitive) to get the same behavior.

docs.title: TransporterType
docs.text:
Available backends for receiving observability events:

Transporter Description TransporterType.HTML Self-contained interactive HTML report (default) TransporterType.JSON JSON file export (full session dump + NDJSON streaming) TransporterType.STRUCTURED_LOG JSON log lines for ELK, Datadog, Splunk, CloudWatch TransporterType.CONSOLE Real-time Rich console output with color-coded events TransporterType.PROMETHEUS Prometheus metrics (counters, histograms) for Grafana TransporterType.OTLP OpenTelemetry span export via OTLP gRPC TransporterType.WEBHOOK HTTP POST each event to a configurable URL TransporterType.CALLBACK Invoke a user-provided Python callable for each event

docs.title: Transporter Classes
docs.text:
Each TransporterType maps to a concrete class in promptise.observability_transporters:

from promptise.observability_transporters import (
    HTMLReportTransporter,
    JSONFileTransporter,
    StructuredLogTransporter,
    ConsoleTransporter,
    PrometheusTransporter,
    OTLPTransporter,
    WebhookTransporter,
    CallbackTransporter,
)
Class Constructor Description HTMLReportTransporter (output_dir="./reports", session_name="promptise") Self-contained HTML report JSONFileTransporter (output_dir="./reports", session_name="promptise", stream=True) NDJSON streaming or full JSON dump StructuredLogTransporter (log_file=None, session_name="promptise", service_name="promptise", correlation_id=None) ELK/Datadog/Splunk-compatible structured logs ConsoleTransporter (live=True, verbose=False) Rich-powered real-time terminal output PrometheusTransporter (port=0) Prometheus metrics endpoint (counters, histograms) OTLPTransporter (endpoint="http://localhost:4317", service_name="promptise") OpenTelemetry spans export WebhookTransporter (url, headers=None, batch_size=0, max_retries=3, timeout=10.0) HTTP POST to external endpoint CallbackTransporter (callback) Invoke custom callable per event

All implement on_event(entry), flush(), and close().

Custom transporter selection:

config = ObservabilityConfig(
    level=ObserveLevel.FULL,
    transporters=[TransporterType.HTML, TransporterType.PROMETHEUS],
)
agent = await build_agent(
    servers=servers, model="openai:gpt-5-mini", observe=config,
)

Custom callback example:

def my_handler(entry):  # entry is a TimelineEntry
    print(f"[{entry.event_type.value}] {entry.agent_id}: {entry.details}")

config = ObservabilityConfig(transporters=[TransporterType.CALLBACK], on_event=my_handler)
# or attach one to an existing collector:
agent.collector.add_transporter(CallbackTransporter(callback=my_handler))

TimelineEntry fields: entry_id, timestamp, event_type, category, agent_id, phase, details (the human-readable text), duration (seconds), parent_id, user_id, session_id, metadata.

docs.title: Configuration Fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description level ObserveLevel STANDARD Detail level session_name str "promptise" Human-readable session identifier (also the OTLP service name and the report/NDJSON file prefix) record_prompts bool \| None None Store prompt/response and agent input/output text. None = only at FULL record_tool_io bool True Store tool arguments, result previews and tool error messages redact_sensitive bool True Replace credentials and common PII in every event with placeholders before it is stored or exported max_entries int 100_000 Max timeline entries before eviction transporters list[TransporterType] [HTML] Active transporters output_dir str \| None None Directory for HTML and JSON output (./reports when unset) log_file str \| None None File path for STRUCTURED_LOG transporter console_live bool False Real-time console printing webhook_url str \| None None Target URL for WEBHOOK transporter webhook_headers dict[str, str] {} Custom HTTP headers for webhooks otlp_endpoint str "http://localhost:4317" gRPC endpoint for OTLP prometheus_port int 9090 Port for Prometheus metrics on_event Callable \| None None User callback for CALLBACK transporter correlation_id str \| None None Added to every structured-log line and OpenTelemetry span

docs.title: PromptiseCallbackHandler
docs.text: PromptiseCallbackHandler is the LangChain callback that bridges LLM events into the observability collector. It is instantiated once per agent and reused across multiple ainvoke() calls.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
from promptise.callback_handler import PromptiseCallbackHandler
from promptise.observability_config import ObserveLevel

handler = PromptiseCallbackHandler(
    collector,                          # ObservabilityCollector instance
    agent_id="my-agent",                # Optional agent identifier for timeline entries
    record_prompts=None,                # None = follow level (text at FULL only)
    level=ObserveLevel.STANDARD,        # Detail level (default: STANDARD)
    record_tool_io=True,                # Tool arguments / result previews (default: True)
)
Parameter Type Default Description collector ObservabilityCollector required The collector that receives timeline events agent_id str \| None None Agent identifier for the collector timeline record_prompts bool \| None None Include prompt/response text; None follows level level ObserveLevel STANDARD OFF (nothing), BASIC (tools + errors), STANDARD (+ LLM turns), FULL (+ text and streamed tokens) record_tool_io bool True Include tool arguments, result previews and error messages

docs.title: Auto-Tracked Events
docs.text:
The handler automatically captures the following without any additional code:

  • LLM turns: Start/end with latency timing, model name extraction
  • Token counts: Prompt tokens, completion tokens, total tokens (from LLMResult and usage_metadata), also added to the current agent run
  • Tool calls: Start/end with tool name, arguments, results, and latency
  • Errors: LLM errors and tool errors (including MCP isError results) with traceback
  • Retries: Retry attempts with attempt number and triggering error
  • Chain events: Top-level input/output when the handler is used on its own (inside a PromptiseAgent, the agent records agent.input / agent.output itself)
  • Streaming tokens: Token-by-token accumulation at FULL level

docs.title: Session Totals
docs.text:
After running the agent, cumulative totals are available on the handler:

Attribute Type Description total_prompt_tokens int Total input tokens total_completion_tokens int Total output tokens total_tokens int Total tokens (prompt + completion) llm_call_count int Number of LLM calls tool_call_count int Number of tool calls error_count int Number of errors retry_count int Number of retries

Use handler.get_summary() to retrieve all metrics as a dict.

docs.title: Post-Run Analysis
docs.text:
After running an agent with observability enabled, use the built-in reporting methods:

# Get runtime statistics
stats = agent.get_stats()

# Write an interactive HTML report
path = agent.generate_report("reports/shop.html", title="Shop assistant — Oct 10")

generate_report(path, title="Agent Observability Report") writes the report to exactly path (creating missing directories, overwriting an existing file) and returns it as a string. It raises RuntimeError when observability is off and OSError when the file cannot be written. The page is self-contained (no network access): stat cards with the same numbers as get_stats(), a timeline you can filter by Agent / LLM / Tool / Error / Cache, and each event's metadata on click.

Separately, the HTML transporter writes <output_dir>/<session_name>-report-<timestamp>.html when the agent shuts down.

docs.title: NDJSON event stream
docs.text: The JSON transporter appends every event as one JSON line to <output_dir>/<session_name>-events.ndjson, and writes a full <session_name>-session-<timestamp>.json dump on shutdown. The NDJSON file is opened in append mode, so every run with the same session_name adds to the same file — useful for tailing and for explain-style scripts, but it grows without limit. Rotate it externally, for example with logrotate and copytruncate.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry traces
docs.text:
The OTLP transporter exports each agent run as one trace:

invoke_agent shop                    3.7 s   enduser.id=customer-42  session.id=q1
├── chat gpt-5-mini                  1.4 s   gen_ai.usage.input_tokens=288
├── execute_tool check_stock         0.8 s   gen_ai.tool.name=check_stock
└── chat gpt-5-mini                  1.5 s
  • The run span lasts from agent.input to agent.output (or agent.error); each LLM call (llm.start → llm.end) and tool call (tool.call → tool.result / tool.error) is a child span with its real start and end time, so span durations are the latencies.
  • Failed tool calls, LLM calls and runs get an ERROR status. Other events of the run (cache hits, retries) are span events on the run span.
  • If an OpenTelemetry span is active when you invoke the agent — say, the server span of an instrumented FastAPI app — the run span becomes its child, so the agent joins the request's trace.
  • Attributes follow the GenAI semantic conventions (gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens, gen_ai.tool.name), plus enduser.id and session.id from the CallerContext, promptise.correlation_id from the config, and every scalar metadata field as promptise.<key>.
  • LLM spans need STANDARD or FULL; at BASIC a run has tool spans only.

OTLPTransporter creates its own TracerProvider and never replaces the global one. To send spans through your application's provider (and its exporters, sampling and resource attributes) instead, attach the transporter yourself:

from opentelemetry import trace
from promptise.observability_transporters import OTLPTransporter

agent.collector.add_transporter(
    OTLPTransporter(tracer_provider=trace.get_tracer_provider(), correlation_id="req-7f3a")
)

docs.title: Enterprise Configuration Example
docs.text:
A production setup with multiple transporters:

from promptise.observability_config import ObservabilityConfig, ObserveLevel, TransporterType

config = ObservabilityConfig(
    level=ObserveLevel.FULL,
    session_name="production-audit",
    record_prompts=True,
    transporters=[
        TransporterType.HTML,
        TransporterType.STRUCTURED_LOG,
        TransporterType.CONSOLE,
        TransporterType.PROMETHEUS,
    ],
    output_dir="./observability",
    log_file="./logs/events.jsonl",
    console_live=True,
    prometheus_port=9090,
    correlation_id="req-abc-123",
)

This configuration:

  • Generates an interactive HTML report in ./observability/
  • Writes structured JSON log lines to ./logs/events.jsonl (compatible with ELK, Datadog, Splunk)
  • Prints color-coded events to the console in real time
  • Exposes Prometheus metrics on port 9090
  • Tags every structured-log line (and, with the OTLP transporter, every span) with the correlation ID req-abc-123

Privacy

Prompt and response text is recorded only at ObserveLevel.FULL or with record_prompts=True; tool arguments and results are recorded unless record_tool_io=False. See What text is recorded. This is particularly important in production environments handling sensitive data.

docs.title: Multi-User Attribution
docs.text:
Every TimelineEntry carries the authenticated caller's user_id and session_id. The ObservabilityCollector reads these automatically from the CallerContext contextvar at record time — there is nothing to wire manually.

from promptise.agent import CallerContext, _caller_ctx_var
from promptise.observability import ObservabilityCollector, TimelineEventType

collector = ObservabilityCollector()
token = _caller_ctx_var.set(CallerContext(user_id="alice", metadata={"session_id": "sess-1"}))
try:
    entry = collector.record(TimelineEventType.TOOL_CALL, details="search(q=...)")
finally:
    _caller_ctx_var.reset(token)

assert entry.user_id == "alice"
assert entry.session_id == "sess-1"

docs.title: Per-tenant queries
docs.text:
Method Returns Description collector.query(user_ids=[...], session_ids=[...]) list[TimelineEntry] Filter the ring buffer by user, session, event type, or time window collector.for_user(user_id) list[TimelineEntry] Shorthand for a single tenant's events collector.get_users() list[str] Unique sorted user_ids present in the buffer collector.purge_user(user_id) int Deletes one user's data on request — drops every entry owned by that user

Entries without a caller (system events like HEALTH_CHECK) keep user_id=None and session_id=None; purge_user never touches them.

TimelineEntry.to_dict() includes both fields, so STRUCTURED_LOG / JSON / WEBHOOK / OTLP transporters all emit per-tenant attribution automatically — no custom transporter code required.

docs.title: Projects & promptise run
docs.text:
A Promptise project works like a Node project. promptise.toml plays the part of package.json: it names the program (main), lists named commands ([scripts]), and says which environment variables the project needs ([env]). promptise run runs your program the way node or npm start would.

Your program stays a normal Python program. Flags add dev tools, a terminal UI, file watching, production behavior or an HTTP API, and with them every agent the program builds is instrumented, with no changes to your code.

promptise init --project my-bot     # create a project
cd my-bot
cp .env.example .env                # then set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env

promptise run                       # run main.py, like `python main.py`
promptise run --devtools            # live traces, tool calls, tokens and cost
promptise run --tui                 # the full terminal UI
promptise run --serve               # an HTTP API for the agent
promptise run --prod                # JSON logs, preflight checks, graceful SIGTERM

A complete example project is in examples/run/support_bot/.

promptise run and promptise runtime

promptise run runs your Python program. For long-running agents that react to triggers (cron, webhooks, file changes) and are declared in .agent manifests, use the Agent Runtime: promptise runtime start agents/ --detach, then promptise runtime status, logs, rewind and stop from any terminal. See the Runtime CLI.

docs.title: How it maps to npm
docs.text:
Node / npm Promptise package.json promptise.toml, or [tool.promptise] in pyproject.toml "main": "index.js" main = "main.py" "scripts": {...} [scripts] node index.js python main.py npm start promptise run (or promptise run start, if you define a start script) npm run dev promptise run dev npm run (lists scripts) promptise run --list npm init promptise init --project nodemon promptise run --watch

The manifest describes how to run the project. The agent itself stays in your Python code.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
promptise init --project [DIR] [--name NAME] [--model MODEL] [--force]
Option Meaning DIR Where to create the project (default: the current directory). Created if missing. --name NAME The project name (default: the directory's name). --model MODEL The model string the agent uses (default: openai:gpt-5-mini). It also decides which API key [env] required lists: anthropic:... gives ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a local ollama:... needs none, and a string without a known provider prefix gives OPENAI_API_KEY. --force Overwrite files that already exist.

It writes:

File Contents promptise.toml name, version = "0.1.0", description, main = "main.py", agent = "agent.py:create_agent", the scripts dev, ui, start, serve and check, [env] required, and a commented-out [pricing] example agent.py create_agent, the agent factory, with one local tool (add) main.py A normal script: builds the agent, asks the question from its arguments (or a default one), prints the answer and shuts the agent down .env.example The variables the model's provider needs README.md How to run the project .gitignore .env, .promptise/ and __pycache__/, added to an existing file without duplicating lines

promptise init --project never overwrites a file without --force. When files exist, it lists every one of them and writes nothing. It never touches the network.

promptise init without --project still writes a .superagent template, as before. See the CLI reference.

docs.title: A project, file by file
docs.text:
This is what promptise init --project creates (comments shortened).

promptise.toml:

name = "my-bot"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "An agent built with Promptise"
main = "main.py"                  # the program `promptise run` runs
agent = "agent.py:create_agent"   # the agent factory for --serve, -i and chat mode

[scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"
ui = "promptise run --tui"
start = "promptise run --prod"
serve = "promptise run --serve"
check = "promptise run --prod --check"

[env]
files = [".env"]
required = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

agent.py, the agent factory:

from __future__ import annotations

from promptise import PromptiseAgent, build_agent, tool
from promptise.run import RunContext

MODEL = "openai:gpt-5-mini"


@tool
def add(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Add two numbers and return the sum."""
    return a + b


async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext | None = None) -> PromptiseAgent:
    model = (ctx.model if ctx is not None else None) or MODEL
    return await build_agent(
        model=model,
        instructions="You are a helpful assistant. Use the add tool for arithmetic.",
        extra_tools=[add],
    )

main.py, the program:

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import sys

from agent import create_agent


async def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "What is 1234 + 5678?"
    agent = await create_agent()
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": question}]
    try:
        result = await agent.ainvoke({"messages": messages})
        print(result["messages"][-1].content)
    finally:
        await agent.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

python main.py and promptise run run the same program. With promptise run, the project's .env and [env] settings are applied, and the agent shows up in the dev tools and the terminal UI.

docs.title: Where promptise run finds it
docs.text:
promptise run looks in the current directory, then in each parent directory. It stops at the first directory that has a promptise.toml, or a pyproject.toml with a [tool.promptise] table. In the same directory, promptise.toml wins. The search also stops at the repository root (the first directory that holds .git), so a manifest above your repository is never used.

-f PATH / --manifest PATH names the manifest explicitly.

The project root is the manifest's directory. Relative paths in the manifest are relative to it.

Without a manifest, promptise run some_file.py still works: the root is the current directory and every setting has its default.

A manifest decides what runs, so promptise run only uses one found this way if it is a regular file owned by you that other users cannot write (the same rule as for .env files). A promptise.toml planted in a shared directory such as /tmp is refused with an error. -f/--manifest uses the file you name.

docs.title: A full example
docs.text:
name = "support-bot"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Answers support tickets"
main = "main.py"
agent = "agent.py:create_agent"
python_path = ["."]

[scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"
ui = "promptise run --tui"
start = "promptise run --prod"
eval = "python evals/run.py"

[env]
files = [".env"]
required = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
vars = { LOG_LEVEL = "info" }

[dev]
observe = "full"
watch = ["."]
ignore = ["data/*"]
report = ".promptise/last-run.json"

[prod]
log_format = "json"
log_level = "INFO"
observe = "off"
shutdown_timeout = 30

[serve]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8080
auth_token_env = "PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN"
max_concurrency = 8

[pricing]
"gpt-5-mini*" = { input = 0.25, output = 2.0 }

Every key is optional. An empty promptise.toml is a valid manifest.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name string the root directory's name The project name, shown in the dev tools, the TUI and /v1/info. version string none The project version. description string none A one-line description. main string the first existing of main.py, agent.py, app.py The program promptise run runs, relative to the root. agent string none An agent factory for the chat, once and serve modes: file.py:function or package.module:function. python_path list of strings ["."] Directories added to sys.path, relative to the root.

docs.title: [scripts]
docs.text: A table of named commands, like npm scripts. Each key is a script name and each value is a command line. A name may not be empty, start with - or contain spaces, and a command may not be empty. See Scripts.

docs.title: [env]
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning files list of strings [".env"] .env-style files to load, in order, relative to the root. A missing file is skipped. required list of strings [] Variables that must be set before the program starts. Every missing one is reported at once. vars table of strings {} Default values, set only when the variable is not set already.

See Environment variables for the loading rules.

docs.title: [dev]
docs.text:
Applies with --devtools, --tui and --watch.

Key Type Default Meaning observe basic, standard or full full How much is recorded for agents that set no observe of their own. --observe LEVEL overrides it. watch list of strings ["."] Paths --watch watches, relative to the root. ignore list of strings [] Extra glob patterns --watch ignores. .git, __pycache__, .venv, venv, node_modules, .promptise, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache and .ruff_cache are always ignored. report string "" Write a JSON run report to this path (relative to the project root) when the run ends. Empty means no report. --report PATH overrides it; that path is relative to the directory you run the command from.

docs.title: [prod]
docs.text:
Applies with --prod.

Key Type Default Meaning log_format json or text json json writes one JSON object per log line on stderr. log_level DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL INFO The root log level (case does not matter). observe off, basic, standard or full off Record agent activity at this level for agents that set no observe of their own. Each timeline event becomes a JSON log line. shutdown_timeout number (seconds) 30 How long in-flight work may take to finish after SIGTERM.

docs.title: [serve]
docs.text:
Applies with --serve. The serve mode needs an agent factory (agent, or a file.py:factory target).

Key Type Default Meaning host string 127.0.0.1 The address to listen on. --host overrides it. port integer, 0 to 65535 8080 The port. --port / -p overrides it. auth_token_env string PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN The environment variable that holds the bearer token clients must send. A token is required when host is not a loopback address. max_concurrency integer, 1 or more 8 Requests answered at the same time. More get 429.

docs.title: [pricing]
docs.text:
Prices for the cost estimates in the dev tools, the TUI and the run report, in USD per one million tokens. Keys are model names, and fnmatch globs are allowed:

[pricing]
"gpt-5-mini*" = { input = 0.25, output = 2.0 }
"claude-sonnet-4-5" = { input = 3.0, output = 15.0 }

A model matches by its exact name first, then by its name without the provider: prefix, then against each glob in table order. Both input and output are required and must be 0 or more.

Promptise has no built-in price list. Prices change, and a wrong number is worse than none. A model without a price shows — instead of a cost and is listed as unpriced. The numbers above are examples: check your provider's current prices.

docs.title: In pyproject.toml
docs.text:
Put the same keys under [tool.promptise], and the sub-tables under [tool.promptise.<name>]:

[tool.promptise]
name = "support-bot"
main = "main.py"
agent = "support_bot.agent:create_agent"

[tool.promptise.scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"

[tool.promptise.env]
required = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

docs.title: Mistakes are errors
docs.text:
An unknown key is an error, so a typo does not go unnoticed. The message names the file and the dotted path of every problem:

/work/support-bot/promptise.toml:
  - dev.obsrve: unknown key (check the spelling)
  - serve.port: Input should be less than or equal to 65535

In pyproject.toml, the paths start with tool.promptise.. promptise run exits with code 2 on a manifest error.

docs.title: Read a manifest from Python
docs.text:
The loader promptise run uses is public in promptise.run, for tools and tests that need the project's settings:

from pathlib import Path
from promptise.run import ManifestError, find_manifest, load_manifest

path = find_manifest(Path.cwd())   # nearest promptise.toml or [tool.promptise], or None
if path is not None:
    try:
        manifest = load_manifest(path)
        print(manifest.name, manifest.main, sorted(manifest.scripts))
    except ManifestError as exc:
        print("\n".join(exc.problems))
Name What it does find_manifest(start=None) The nearest manifest from start (default: the working directory) upwards, or None. In each directory promptise.toml wins over a pyproject.toml with [tool.promptise]. The search stops at the first directory holding .git. load_manifest(path) Read and validate the file and return a ProjectManifest (name, version, description, main, agent, python_path, scripts, env, dev, prod, serve, pricing, path, root). ManifestError Raised when the file cannot be read, parsed or validated; problems lists one line per problem.

docs.title: main and the agent factory
docs.text:
A project can name two things: a program (main) and an agent factory (agent).

  • main is your program. It does whatever your application does: answer a batch of tickets, run a pipeline, start a bot. promptise run runs it like python main.py.
  • agent is a function that builds and returns one agent. promptise run uses it when it drives the agent: the interactive chat, a one-shot question (-i) and the HTTP API (--serve).

Most projects have both: main.py imports the factory from agent.py, so the program and the HTTP API use the same agent.

docs.title: main: your program
docs.text:
promptise run runs main as a complete program, with the same semantics as python main.py:

  • It runs as __main__, so if __name__ == "__main__": blocks run.
  • sys.argv is [main, *ARGS]: the arguments after the target.
  • sys.path[0] is the main file's directory, followed by the root and the python_path entries.
  • The working directory is the project root when a manifest was found. The directory you ran promptise run from is in PROMPTISE_INIT_CWD.
  • sys.exit(code) sets the exit code. Ctrl+C gives 130. An uncaught exception gives 1 (with a readable traceback in dev mode).

Every agent the program builds with build_agent() is instrumented: it appears in the dev tools, the TUI and the run report. See What promptise run adds.

docs.title: The agent factory
docs.text:
A factory is a function that returns a PromptiseAgent. It may be sync or async, and it takes either no argument or a RunContext:

from promptise import PromptiseAgent, build_agent
from promptise.run import RunContext


async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext) -> PromptiseAgent:
    return await build_agent(model=ctx.model or "openai:gpt-5-mini", instructions="...")

A factory that also runs outside promptise run (called from main.py, say) can make the context optional: async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext | None = None). promptise run still passes the context.

The factory must build the agent when it is called. If the name points to an agent that was already built when the module was imported, promptise run refuses it with a message that says so, because it must build the agent inside its own event loop. promptise run calls await agent.shutdown() when the run ends.

RunContext is a frozen dataclass in promptise.run:

Field Type Meaning project str The project name. root Path The project root. mode "script", "chat", "once" or "serve" The mode of this run. devtools bool --devtools (or --tui) is on. prod bool --prod is on. tui bool The run is shown in the terminal UI. model str or None The --model override. promptise run applies it to every agent anyway, so a factory only needs it to pick a model-specific setting. manifest ProjectManifest or None The parsed manifest. args tuple[str, ...] The arguments after the target.

docs.title: Targets and modes
docs.text:
promptise run [TARGET] [ARGS]... [OPTIONS]

TARGET is one of these, checked in this order:

  1. Omitted: the manifest's main.
  2. A name in [scripts]: run that script. See Scripts.
  3. A .py file: run that file instead of main, with the manifest's settings.
  4. file.py:factory or package.module:factory: use that agent factory.

ARGS become the program's sys.argv[1:]. To pass arguments to main, name the file:

promptise run main.py "Where is my order A1002?"

Put -- before arguments that look like promptise run options, so they reach your program unchanged: promptise run main.py -- --verbose.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Mode What runs Use it for script The program, as __main__ Running your application chat The factory's agent, in an interactive chat in the terminal Trying the agent by hand once The factory's agent, for one question; the answer is printed and the process exits Shell scripts, CI checks serve The factory's agent, behind an HTTP API Other services calling the agent

--mode auto (the default) picks the mode:

  1. An explicit :factory target, --serve or -i gives an agent mode (chat, serve or once).
  2. Otherwise, if the main file has an if __name__ == "__main__": block, or top-level statements other than imports, definitions and assignments (asyncio.run(main())), it runs as a script.
  3. Otherwise, if it defines create_agent, it opens the chat.
  4. Otherwise it runs as a script.

Set the mode yourself with --mode script|chat|once|serve. --serve is short for --mode serve, and -i TEXT / --input TEXT is short for --mode once with that question.

docs.title: Chat mode
docs.text:
promptise run --mode chat                 # the manifest's agent factory
promptise run agent.py:create_agent       # a factory named on the command line

The answer streams as it is written, and tool calls appear inline. Commands:

Command What it does /help List the commands /stats Tokens, cost and tool calls so far /tools The agent's tools /reset Start a new conversation /exit Quit (also Ctrl+D)

docs.title: Once mode
docs.text:
promptise run -i "Where is my order A1002?"
echo "Where is my order A1002?" | promptise run -i -     # read the question from stdin
promptise run -i "Where is my order A1002?" --json       # the answer and stats as JSON

docs.title: What promptise run adds to your agents
docs.text:
A plain promptise run of a script adds nothing to your agents: the program runs exactly as with python main.py, plus the project's environment, at no extra cost.

With --devtools, --tui, --model, --observe, --report or [prod] observe, and in the chat, once and serve modes, promptise run installs a harness before your program starts. build_agent() asks it for settings and reports every agent it builds. With the harness, promptise run:

  • turns on observability, at the run's level, for agents that set no observe of their own, without writing report files;
  • gives each agent an id (agent, agent-2, ...) when it has none;
  • adds a sink for agent events, creating an EventNotifier when the agent has none;
  • replaces every agent's model with the --model override, when you give one;
  • reports each agent's model, tools, MCP servers and features to the dev tools and the TUI.

Your values always win. An agent built with observe=False stays unobserved. One with its own observe config keeps it, and its own events notifier keeps working, with the run's sink added to it.

Outside promptise run, nothing changes: python main.py builds the same agents with no harness.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
[scripts] holds named commands, like npm scripts:

[scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"
ui = "promptise run --tui"
start = "promptise run --prod"
eval = "python evals/run.py"
lint = "ruff check ."

promptise run dev           # promptise run --devtools --watch
promptise run eval smoke    # python evals/run.py smoke
promptise run --list        # list the scripts
  • A script runs through the shell, from the project root. Its exit code is the exit code of promptise run.
  • Arguments after the script name are appended to the command. Put -- before arguments that look like promptise run options: promptise run eval -- --limit 10.
  • promptise run options given with the script name are passed on when the script is itself a promptise command: promptise run dev --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5 runs promptise run --devtools --watch --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5. For any other command they are ignored, with a warning.
  • The directory of the Python that runs promptise comes first on PATH, so python, pytest and promptise in a script are the ones from the same environment. This works like node_modules/.bin in npm.
  • The script gets PROMPTISE_RUN_SCRIPT (its name), PROMPTISE_PROJECT_ROOT and PROMPTISE_INIT_CWD (the directory you ran promptise run from).
  • [env] is applied by promptise run itself, so a script that runs promptise run gets it. Other commands get the environment you started with.
  • A script that calls itself through promptise run stops with an error instead of looping forever.
  • When the command is echoed, the values of --env KEY=VALUE are shown as ***.
  • On Windows, scripts run through cmd.exe, which has no quoting that is safe for every character: an appended argument that contains & | < > ^ % ! " is refused. Run such a command directly.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Before the program starts, promptise run sets up its environment:

  1. Command line. -e K=V / --env K=V (repeatable) sets a variable for this run. It wins over everything, including a variable already set in your shell.
  2. Files. The --env-file PATH files (repeatable) load first, then the [env] files (default [".env"]), in order. A missing --env-file is an error; a missing file in [env] files is skipped.
  3. Defaults. [env] vars fills in variables that are still not set.
  4. Check. Every variable in [env] required must be set. If any are missing, promptise run lists all of them and exits with code 2.

The rules:

  • A file never overrides. A variable that is already set to a non-empty value is never changed by a file or by [env] vars, so the first file that sets a variable wins. A variable exported as an empty string (export OPENAI_API_KEY=) counts as not set, so a file's value fills it.
  • Unsafe files are refused. A file must be a regular file. On Linux and macOS it must be owned by you and not writable by other users. An unsafe or unreadable file is an error that names the file.
  • PROMPTISE_NO_DOTENV=1 turns file loading off. No .env-style file is loaded. Use it in containers and CI, where the environment is set from outside.

The CLI also loads a .env from the current directory (or a parent, up to the project root) before any command runs, under the same rules. See Configuration & Secrets.

promptise run never shows variable values. The TUI and the run report list only whether each variable is set.

docs.title: Dev tools
docs.text:
promptise run --devtools     # or -d

--devtools prints a live trace of every agent on stderr. Your program's own output stays on stdout, unchanged. The trace shows:

  • each agent as it is built: its model and tools;
  • every LLM turn: model, latency, tokens, estimated cost and the tools it asked for;
  • every tool call, with its arguments and a preview of the result;
  • errors and notable agent events (a guardrail block, a slow tool, an approval request).

When the run ends, a summary table lists the totals per agent, per model and per tool: LLM calls, tokens, tool calls, errors, latency and cost.

promptise run --devtools on the support bot example. The trace goes to stderr; the program's answer is its own output. Setting Effect [dev] observe / --observe LEVEL How much is recorded: basic, standard or full (default). [dev] report / --report PATH Write a JSON run report on exit: every run event that was kept, and the final totals. [pricing] The prices behind the cost estimates.

Costs are estimates from your [pricing] table. A model without a price shows —.

docs.title: Watch mode
docs.text:
promptise run --watch            # or -w
promptise run --devtools --watch # the `dev` script of a new project

--watch runs the program in a child process and restarts it when a project file changes, like nodemon. Changes are debounced, so saving several files restarts once. When the program exits on its own, promptise run waits for the next change and runs it again. --watch is for development: it cannot be combined with --prod.

  • Watched: the paths in [dev] watch (default: the whole root).
  • File types: .py, .toml, .yaml, .yml, .json, .md, .txt, .env, .j2, .jinja, .agent and .superagent.
  • Ignored: .git, __pycache__, .venv, venv, node_modules, .promptise, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache, and the globs in [dev] ignore.

docs.title: The terminal UI
docs.text:
promptise run --tui      # also -t or -tui
promptise run ui         # the `ui` script of a new project

--tui opens a full-screen terminal UI. It records what --devtools records and shows it in tabs. The program runs in a child process, and its output is captured line by line, so nothing it prints draws over the UI.

In script mode, the first tab is a console: it shows the program's output, and a line you type is sent to the program's standard input. In the agent modes (--mode chat, --serve), the first tab is a chat with the agent.

The Chat tab of the support bot example (promptise run --tui --mode chat). Tool calls show inline, with their arguments, results and timings. Key Tab Shows 1 Console / Chat The program's output and input, or the chat with the agent (streamed answers, tool calls inline) 2 Trace Every timeline entry of every agent (LLM calls, tool calls and results, errors, with timings), filterable by agent, with the full entry beside it 3 Tools Every tool call (arguments, result, latency) and the tools each agent has 4 Metrics Totals, per agent, model and tool, and the tokens of each LLM call 5 Events Agent events: invocations, slow tools, guardrails, approvals 6 Approvals Tool calls waiting for a human decision, and the decisions made 7 Agents Every agent the program built: model, observability level, tools, MCP servers, features and instructions 8 MCP The MCP servers the agents use, with their transport and tools 9 Logs Python log records and the program's stderr, filterable by level 0 Run The project, the entry, the mode and flags, the manifest, the environment variables (set or missing, never their values), the scripts, HTTP requests in serve mode, and the run's state and exit code Key Action 0 to 9 Switch tabs (when the input box does not have focus) esc Leave the input box r Restart the program s Stop the program a / d Approvals tab: approve or deny the selected request (deny asks for an optional reason) a Trace tab: filter by agent l Logs tab: filter by level ? Help q, Ctrl+C Quit

Trace: every LLM call and tool call of every agent, with the full entry beside the table.

Tools: every call with its arguments and result, and the tools each agent can use.

Metrics: totals, latency, tokens per call, and the breakdown per agent, model and tool.

Approvals: a tool call waiting for a person. a approves, d denies. Personal data in the arguments is redacted.

Agents: what each agent was built with.

Run: the project, the process, the environment (names only) and the manifest.

The Approvals tab answers requests from agents whose approval policy uses a QueueApprovalHandler. Other handlers (webhooks, callbacks) already have someone answering them and are left alone. See Approval (HITL).

Add --watch (promptise run --tui --watch) and the program restarts in the UI whenever a watched file changes; the run history stays, and each run is numbered.

--tui needs an interactive terminal. It cannot be combined with --prod.

docs.title: Production
docs.text:
promptise run --prod            # or `promptise run start` in a new project
promptise run --prod --check    # check the project, then exit

--prod is for running the project unattended, in a container or under a process manager.

  • JSON logs on stderr. Every log record becomes one JSON object per line: ts, level, logger, msg, and any extra fields (exc for a traceback). Stdout stays your program's output. Set [prod] log_format = "text" for plain lines and [prod] log_level for the level.
  • Run events in the logs. The start and the end of the run are written as JSON log lines ("logger": "promptise.run.events"). When agents are instrumented (in serve mode, or with [prod] observe set), so are every agent built and closed, every HTTP request, and the final totals. With [prod] observe, every timeline event (LLM calls, tool calls, errors) is written too.
  • Checks before the start. See Preflight checks. Under --prod, the problems are written as one JSON log line ("msg": "preflight failed", "problems": [...]).
  • Graceful SIGTERM. On SIGTERM, a script shuts down the way it does on Ctrl+C: it sees KeyboardInterrupt, asyncio.run cancels its main task, finally blocks run and agents shut down. The exit code is 143. In serve mode the server drains instead (see Limits and shutdown) and exits with 0. A second SIGTERM exits at once.

--prod cannot be combined with --tui or --watch.

docs.title: Preflight checks
docs.text:
Every promptise run checks the project before it starts the program, and lists every problem it found instead of failing on the first one at runtime:

  • the manifest is valid;
  • every -e K=V is well formed, every --env-file exists, and every env file can be read and is safe to load;
  • every variable in [env] required is set;
  • the entry exists: the main file, or the agent factory for the agent modes.

If anything is wrong, it exits with code 2 and starts nothing.

--check runs the same checks and also checks the entry itself: a script must compile, and a factory's module must import and define the factory. Then it exits: 0 when the project is ready, 2 when it is not. Importing a factory module runs its module-level code; a script is only compiled, never run.

promptise run --check                    # main
promptise run --prod --serve --check     # what the container will run

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 The program finished, or the server shut down cleanly 1 A runtime error: an uncaught exception, a factory that failed to build the agent, a port that is in use 2 A configuration or usage error: an invalid manifest, a missing variable, an unknown target, a failed check, a public host without a token 130 Interrupted with Ctrl+C 143 Stopped by SIGTERM (script mode, with --prod)

In script mode, sys.exit(code) in your program sets the code.

docs.title: Serve mode
docs.text:
promptise run --serve                       # 127.0.0.1:8080, from [serve]
promptise run --serve --port 9000
promptise run --prod --serve --host 0.0.0.0 # in a container (needs a token)

--serve builds the agent from the factory and answers HTTP requests. One agent serves every request.

Method and path Auth Response GET /healthz none 200 {"status": "ok"} while the process runs (liveness) GET /readyz none 200 {"status": "ready"} once the agent is built; 503 before that (not_ready) and while shutting down (draining) (readiness) GET /v1/info bearer The project (name, version, model, ...) and the agent's tool names POST /v1/invoke bearer Runs the agent: {"output", "duration_ms", "usage", "request_id"} POST /v1/stream bearer Runs the agent and streams Server-Sent Events, one data: <JSON> line per event

The request body of /v1/invoke and /v1/stream is a JSON object:

Field Type Meaning input string, or a list of messages The question, or the conversation as [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}] session_id string, optional 1 to 256 letters, digits, ., _, : or -

With a string input and a session_id, an agent built with a conversation_store loads and saves the conversation of that session, so the client sends only the new message. Otherwise nothing is stored: with a list of messages, the client owns the history. See Conversations.

curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/info

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/invoke \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "Where is my order A1002?"}'

{
  "output": "Your order A1002 is in transit with DHL and should arrive on 2026-10-19.",
  "duration_ms": 2140.5,
  "usage": {"llm_calls": 2, "prompt_tokens": 1630, "completion_tokens": 58, "total_tokens": 1688},
  "request_id": "6f1d0c9e2a7b4c1e"
}

usage counts the tokens of every model call the request made, as the model reported them (zeros when it reports none).

curl -N localhost:8080/v1/stream \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "Where is my order A1002?"}'

Each streamed event is a streaming event as JSON. Its type is token, tool_start or tool_end, and the stream ends with done (which also carries usage) or error:

data: {"type": "tool_start", "tool_name": "lookup_order", "arguments": {"order_id": "A1002"}, ...}
data: {"type": "tool_end", "tool_name": "lookup_order", "success": true, "duration_ms": 3.1, ...}
data: {"type": "token", "text": "Your order", ...}
data: {"type": "done", "full_response": "Your order A1002 is in transit ...", "usage": {...}, ...}

A streamed request with a stored session (session_id on an agent with a conversation_store) sends the whole answer as one token event, then done.

Every response has an X-Request-ID header: the one the client sent, when it is well formed, or a new one.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
When the variable named by [serve] auth_token_env (default PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN) is set, every /v1/* request must send it as a bearer token, or it gets 401. /healthz and /readyz never need one, so probes work without it. Use a long random token: a token shorter than 16 characters logs a warning.

export PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
promptise run --serve

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/invoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "Where is my order A1002?"}'

On a host that is not a loopback address (--host 0.0.0.0, say), promptise run refuses to start without a token (exit code 2).

Without a token, on a loopback address, /v1/* refuses a request whose Host header is not a loopback name (421) or that carries a cross-site Origin (403). A web page open in your browser cannot drive the agent.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors are JSON: {"error": "<message>"}.

Status When 400 The body is not a JSON object, has unknown fields, or has an invalid input or session_id 401 A token is set and the request has no valid bearer token 403, 421 No token is set and the request comes from a browser page or a non-loopback Host 429 {"error": "busy"}: max_concurrency requests are already running (with Retry-After) 500 {"error": "internal error", "error_id": "..."}: the agent failed. The exception is logged with the same error_id, never sent to the client 503 {"error": "draining"}: the server is shutting down

docs.title: Limits and shutdown
docs.text:
• At most [serve] max_concurrency requests (default 8) run at the same time. A request beyond that gets 429 at once.
  • On SIGTERM (or Ctrl+C) the server drains: /readyz and new /v1/* requests answer 503, and requests already running get up to [prod] shutdown_timeout seconds to finish. Then the process exits with 0.

The API serves one agent for one application. To give each of your users their own identity, conversations and permissions, embed the agent in your own web server instead.

docs.title: Deploy with Docker
docs.text:
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir promptise
COPY . .

# The environment comes from the container, not from a .env file.
ENV PROMPTISE_NO_DOTENV=1

EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["promptise", "run", "--prod", "--serve", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]

Pass the API key and the serve token as environment variables, not in the image:

docker build -t support-bot .
docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  -e OPENAI_API_KEY \
  -e PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN \
  support-bot

Because the host is 0.0.0.0, the container refuses to start without PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN. Point the liveness probe at /healthz and the readiness probe at /readyz. The container stops gracefully on SIGTERM, which is what docker stop and Kubernetes send.

Add a .dockerignore with .env so your local secrets never end up in the image. To check a project before you deploy it, run promptise run --prod --check in CI with the same environment variables.

docs.title: Migrating from promptise run --model-id
docs.text:
The inline REPL still works unchanged:

promptise run --model-id openai:gpt-5-mini \
    --http "name=tools url=http://localhost:8000/mcp"

--model-id, --stdio, --http, --instructions, --trace/--no-trace and --raw/--no-raw select it, exactly as in 1.3. You do not need to change anything.

To move the same setup into a project, put the servers in a factory:

from promptise import PromptiseAgent, build_agent
from promptise.config import HTTPServerSpec
from promptise.run import RunContext


async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext) -> PromptiseAgent:
    return await build_agent(
        model=ctx.model or "openai:gpt-5-mini",
        servers={"tools": HTTPServerSpec(url="http://localhost:8000/mcp")},
    )
Before After promptise run --model-id M --http "..." promptise run agent.py:create_agent (chat mode), or promptise run --mode chat with agent = "agent.py:create_agent" in the manifest --model-id M --model M (overrides the model of every agent) --instructions "..." instructions= in build_agent() --trace --devtools

docs.title: Flag reference
docs.text: Flag Meaning TARGET A script name, a .py file, file.py:factory or package.module:factory (default: main) ARGS Arguments for the program (sys.argv[1:]) or appended to a script; -- ends the options -d, --devtools Dev tools: live trace on stderr and a summary at the end -t, -tui, --tui The terminal UI -w, --watch Restart on file changes --prod Production behavior; not with --tui or --watch --check Check the project and the entry, then exit 0 (ready) or 2 --mode MODE auto (default), script, chat, once or serve --serve Short for --mode serve -i TEXT, --input TEXT Ask one question (once mode); - reads it from stdin --json Once mode: print the answer and stats as JSON --host HOST Serve mode: the address (overrides [serve] host) -p PORT, --port PORT Serve mode: the port (overrides [serve] port) --env-file PATH Load this .env-style file before the [env] files (repeatable) -e K=V, --env K=V Set a variable for this run, overriding the environment (repeatable) --model MODEL Use this model for every agent --observe LEVEL Override [dev] observe or [prod] observe --report PATH Write a JSON run report on exit --list List the scripts -f PATH, --manifest PATH Use this manifest

  • How to Deploy an AI Agent with Docker (2026 Guide): Dockerfile, secrets, health checks and graceful shutdown.

docs.title: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
docs.text:
A small, pluggable foundation for adding document retrieval to Promptise agents. The framework ships with base classes you subclass for your own loader, chunker, embedder, and vector store, plus a batteries-included reference implementation (in-memory store + recursive text chunker) you can use immediately or swap out piece by piece as you productionise.

from promptise import (
    build_agent,
    RAGPipeline,
    RecursiveTextChunker,
    InMemoryVectorStore,
    rag_to_tool,
)
from promptise.config import HTTPServerSpec

# Your code: plug in a loader + embedder
pipeline = RAGPipeline(
    loader=MyMarkdownLoader("./knowledge_base"),
    chunker=RecursiveTextChunker(chunk_size=800, overlap=100),
    embedder=MyOpenAIEmbedder(),
    store=InMemoryVectorStore(),
)
await pipeline.index()

# Expose retrieval as a tool the agent can call
docs_tool = rag_to_tool(
    pipeline,
    name="search_internal_docs",
    description="Search Acme Corp's engineering wiki.",
)

agent = await build_agent(
    model="openai:gpt-5-mini",
    servers={"tools": HTTPServerSpec(url="http://localhost:8000/mcp")},
    extra_tools=[docs_tool],
)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────────┐
│ DocumentLoader│-->│ Chunker │-->│ Embedder │-->│ VectorStore │
└──────────────┘   └──────────┘   └──────────┘   └──────────────┘
                                                        │
                                                        v
                                                  rag_to_tool()
                                                        │
                                                        v
                                                  LangChain Tool
                                                        │
                                                        v
                                                    Your Agent

Four base classes, a pipeline orchestrator, and a tool adapter. That's it. Each base class has one or two methods: override them, ship your own implementation, and pass it to RAGPipeline.

docs.title: Core Data Types
docs.text:
Type Purpose Document A raw text document with id, text, and metadata. Whatever your loader produces. Chunk A piece of a document with id, document_id, text, optional embedding, and metadata. Produced by the chunker. RetrievalResult A chunk plus a score in [0.0, 1.0]. Returned by search() and retrieve(). IndexReport Summary of pipeline.index(): documents loaded, chunks created, chunks stored, errors, duration.

All four are @dataclass-based: cheap to construct, easy to pickle, introspectable.

docs.title: DocumentLoader
docs.text:
Load raw documents from wherever they live: filesystem, S3, Notion, Confluence, Postgres, a REST API. Override one of two methods:

class DocumentLoader:
    async def load(self) -> list[Document]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def iter_load(self) -> AsyncIterator[Document]:
        for doc in await self.load():   # default: yields from load()
            yield doc

Override load() for sources that fit in memory, or iter_load() to stream a large source one document at a time.

Example, loading markdown files from disk:

from pathlib import Path
from promptise.rag import Document, DocumentLoader

class MarkdownLoader(DocumentLoader):
    def __init__(self, root: str) -> None:
        self.root = Path(root)

    async def load(self) -> list[Document]:
        return [
            Document(
                id=str(p.relative_to(self.root)),
                text=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                metadata={"source": str(p), "title": p.stem},
            )
            for p in self.root.rglob("*.md")
        ]

That's it. During index() the pipeline reads the loader through iter_load() (which calls load() unless you override it) and feeds the documents to the chunker, about batch_size chunks at a time.

docs.title: Chunker
docs.text:
Split documents into retrievable chunks. The base class:

class Chunker:
    async def chunk(self, document: Document) -> list[Chunk]:
        raise NotImplementedError

Built-in: RecursiveTextChunker: splits on natural separators (\n\n, \n, ., ) with configurable chunk_size and overlap. Good default for prose, markdown, and code.

from promptise import RecursiveTextChunker

chunker = RecursiveTextChunker(
    chunk_size=800,       # target chars per chunk
    overlap=100,          # overlap between consecutive chunks
    separators=None,      # defaults to ["\n\n", "\n", ". ", " "]
)

When no separator splits a piece small enough, the piece is cut into chunk_size-character windows that share overlap characters. An empty string "" in separators means that character-level cut, so LangChain-style lists such as ["\n\n", "\n", " ", ""] work. overlap must be smaller than chunk_size. Empty and whitespace-only documents produce no chunks.

Chunk IDs are deterministic ({document_id}:chunk-{i}) so re-indexing the same document produces stable IDs: useful for incremental updates (see Updating documents).

Rolling your own is ~20 lines. Subclass Chunker and return a list of Chunk objects with document_id, text, and any metadata you want to pass through.

docs.title: Embedder
docs.text:
Turn text into dense vectors. The base class has one method plus one property:

class Embedder:
    async def embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    @property
    def dimension(self) -> int:
        raise NotImplementedError

Example, OpenAI embeddings:

from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from promptise.rag import Embedder

class OpenAIEmbedder(Embedder):
    def __init__(self, model: str = "text-embedding-3-small") -> None:
        self.client = AsyncOpenAI()
        self.model = model
        self._dim = 1536 if "small" in model else 3072

    async def embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        resp = await self.client.embeddings.create(
            model=self.model,
            input=texts,
        )
        return [d.embedding for d in resp.data]

    @property
    def dimension(self) -> int:
        return self._dim

Swap for Cohere, VoyageAI, sentence-transformers, Ollama, or an air-gapped local model by changing this one class.

docs.title: VectorStore
docs.text:
Persist chunks and serve similarity queries. The base class:

class VectorStore:
    async def add(self, chunks: list[Chunk]) -> None: ...
    async def search(
        self,
        vector: list[float],
        *,
        limit: int = 5,
        filter: dict | None = None,
    ) -> list[RetrievalResult]: ...
    async def delete(self, chunk_ids: list[str]) -> None: ...
    async def delete_by_document(self, document_id: str) -> int: ...
    async def count(self) -> int: ...
    async def close(self) -> None: ...

Built-in: InMemoryVectorStore: cosine-similarity over an in-process list. Zero external dependencies, no persistence. Great for tests, notebooks, and small corpora (< ~10k chunks). When you outgrow it, subclass and wire up Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, pgvector, Milvus, or Chroma.

from promptise import InMemoryVectorStore

store = InMemoryVectorStore(dimension=1536)  # optional dimension enforcement

Scores are cosine similarity mapped from [-1, 1] onto [0, 1] as (cosine + 1) / 2: an identical direction scores 1.0 and an unrelated (orthogonal) chunk scores 0.5. A query vector whose length differs from the stored vectors (or from dimension) raises ValueError: the query and the index must come from the same embedder. A non-positive limit returns no results. Results are copies, so changing one never changes the stored chunk.

Rolling your own means implementing add, search, and delete against your backend. ~50-100 lines for most vector DBs.

docs.title: RAGPipeline
docs.text:
The orchestrator. Ties a loader + chunker + embedder + store together and exposes two operations: index() (build the index) and retrieve() (query it).

pipeline = RAGPipeline(
    loader=MyLoader(),
    chunker=RecursiveTextChunker(chunk_size=800, overlap=100),
    embedder=MyEmbedder(),
    store=InMemoryVectorStore(),
)

# Ingest everything from the loader
report = await pipeline.index()
print(f"Indexed {report.documents_loaded} docs -> {report.chunks_stored} chunks")
print(f"Duration: {report.duration_seconds:.2f}s")

# Retrieve
results = await pipeline.retrieve("how do I configure memory?", limit=5)
for r in results:
    print(f"[{r.score:.2f}] {r.metadata.get('source')}: {r.text[:80]}")

docs.title: Incremental indexing
docs.text:
Pass explicit documents to skip the loader for ad-hoc ingestion:

from promptise import Document

await pipeline.index(documents=[
    Document(id="note-1", text="Meeting notes: ..."),
])

docs.title: Updating documents
docs.text:
Indexing a document whose id is already in the store replaces it: the pipeline removes the document's old chunks, then stores the new ones, so text you removed from a document can no longer be retrieved. If the new version's chunks fail to embed, the old version stays and the failure is in report.errors. When the same id appears twice in one index() call, the last one wins.

Removing old chunks uses VectorStore.delete_by_document(). If your store doesn't implement it, the pipeline deletes the chunk ids it stored for that document itself, which only covers documents indexed by the same RAGPipeline instance, so implement delete_by_document() on a persistent store.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text:
Remove a document and all its chunks:

removed = await pipeline.delete_document("note-1")

This uses the same removal as an update, and returns 0 (with a warning) when the store has no delete_by_document() and the pipeline never indexed the document.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text: Chunker defaults to RecursiveTextChunker(chunk_size=500, overlap=50) if you don't supply one, and batch_size (chunks per embed() call) defaults to 64. embedder and store are required; loader is only needed when you call index() without documents.

docs.title: rag_to_tool: expose retrieval to an agent
docs.text:
The glue that turns a RAGPipeline into a LangChain tool the agent can call via extra_tools. The agent sees a single tool with a query argument; calling it runs retrieval and returns formatted results.

from promptise import rag_to_tool

docs_tool = rag_to_tool(
    pipeline,
    name="search_product_docs",
    description="Search Acme Corp's product documentation. Use for how-to questions.",
    limit=5,
    format="markdown",  # "markdown" (default), "json", or "text"
)
Parameter Default Purpose name "search_knowledge_base" Tool name the LLM sees. Make it specific. description Generic What's in the knowledge base. The LLM uses this to decide when to call the tool. limit 5 Default result count (at least 1). The LLM can override it with any value of 1 or more. format "markdown" How results are returned to the LLM. Any other value raises ValueError.

Format cheat sheet:

  • "markdown": human + LLM friendly, includes source and title headers
  • "json", structured: {"notice": ..., "results": [{score, text, metadata}, ...]}, best for downstream processing
  • "text": plain text with source prefix, minimal token overhead

Retrieved text is untrusted. Anyone who can put text into an indexed document (a wiki editor, a customer filing a ticket) can write instructions aimed at the model. The tool output says that the results are data, not instructions to follow. In "markdown" and "text" the results sit inside a block delimited by a random tag generated for each call (<retrieved-documents-…>), so a document can't close the block early and pose as the tool's own output; in "json" the notice field carries the same statement. This lowers the risk but doesn't remove it: keep side-effecting tools behind approval when the agent also reads documents that outsiders can write.

docs.title: Content hashing for dedup
docs.text:
Use content_hash() as part of your document ID to detect unchanged documents and skip re-embedding:

from promptise.rag import content_hash

doc_id = f"{source_path}:{content_hash(text)}"

The hash is a stable 12-character string derived from the text: same text always hashes to the same value.

docs.title: Metadata filtering
docs.text:
InMemoryVectorStore.search() (and pipeline.retrieve(..., filter=...)) supports exact-match metadata filters: every key must be present on the chunk with an equal value, so {"tenant_id": None} does not match chunks that have no tenant_id. Your custom stores should do the same:

results = await store.search(
    query_embedding,
    limit=5,
    filter={"category": "support", "status": "published"},
)

docs.title: Who can retrieve what
docs.text:
A RAGPipeline is one shared corpus, and rag_to_tool() does not scope results to the caller: every caller of an agent that has the tool can retrieve every document in the pipeline. Index only documents that every caller may read. For per-user facts, use a memory provider with MemoryScope.PER_USER, which is scoped to the caller automatically.

To keep several tenants' documents in one store, tag each document with its owner and write the tool yourself with @tool, filtering on the caller of the current request. A CallerContext | None parameter receives the CallerContext passed to ainvoke() / chat() (None when there is none, and the model never sees or sets it), and the tool must refuse when there is none:

from promptise import CallerContext, tool

await pipeline.index(documents=[
    Document(id="acme-sla", text="Our SLA is 4 hours.", metadata={"tenant_id": "acme"}),
])

@tool
async def search_my_docs(query: str, caller: CallerContext | None) -> str:
    """Search the documents of the caller's organisation."""
    if caller is None or caller.tenant_id is None:
        return "No tenant for this request; search refused."
    hits = await pipeline.retrieve(query, limit=5, filter={"tenant_id": caller.tenant_id})
    return "\n\n".join(h.text for h in hits) or "No relevant results found."

agent = await build_agent(model="openai:gpt-5-mini", extra_tools=[search_my_docs])

A tool you write yourself doesn't get rag_to_tool()'s untrusted-data block; add the same kind of notice to its output.

docs.title: Hybrid search
docs.text: VectorStore is just a protocol. Subclass to add BM25, reranking, recency boosts, or any hybrid strategy. Return RetrievalResult with your combined score.

docs.title: Multi-store composition
docs.text:
Run multiple pipelines for different corpora and expose each as its own tool. The agent picks the right one based on the description:

docs_tool = rag_to_tool(docs_pipeline, name="search_docs", description="Product docs.")
tickets_tool = rag_to_tool(tickets_pipeline, name="search_tickets", description="Support tickets.")

agent = await build_agent(
    model="openai:gpt-5-mini",
    servers={},
    extra_tools=[docs_tool, tickets_tool],
)

docs.title: When to use RAG vs. Memory
docs.text:
Both inject external context into the LLM. Different lifecycles:

RAG Memory Source Your documents (filesystem, wiki, tickets) Conversation history, facts the agent observed Write path Offline indexing Live during agent runs Trigger LLM explicitly calls the tool Auto-injected before every invocation Scale Millions of chunks Thousands of memories per user Typical use "What's our refund policy?" "User's preferred deployment target is GKE"

Use both together: memory for who the user is, RAG for what the knowledge base says.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The in-memory components are designed for tests: zero dependencies, deterministic behavior. Wire them up with a fake embedder and you've got an end-to-end RAG test in ~20 lines:

from promptise.rag import (
    Document,
    Embedder,
    InMemoryVectorStore,
    RAGPipeline,
    RecursiveTextChunker,
)

class FakeEmbedder(Embedder):
    async def embed(self, texts):
        return [[float(len(t) % 10) / 10, float(t.count("a")) / max(len(t), 1)] for t in texts]

    @property
    def dimension(self):
        return 2

async def test_retrieval():
    pipeline = RAGPipeline(
        chunker=RecursiveTextChunker(chunk_size=200),
        embedder=FakeEmbedder(),
        store=InMemoryVectorStore(),
    )
    await pipeline.index(documents=[
        Document(id="d1", text="The capital of France is Paris."),
    ])
    results = await pipeline.retrieve("France capital")
    assert any("Paris" in r.text for r in results)

See tests/test_rag.py in the repo for the full test suite.
